articles.title: How will El Niño affect winter weather in the US and which states could see the biggest changes?
articles.standfirst: NOAA’s October update points to a strengthening El Niño through early 2027
articles.summary: NOAA’s October update points to a strengthening El Niño through early 2027
articles.body:
For families planning holiday travel or getting their homes ready for winter, the latest El Niño forecast offers an early signal of what could be ahead. Southern states face increased odds of wetter conditions, while much of the northern United States leans toward a warmer season. Those shifts matter, but they do not tell residents when the next storm will arrive or whether their neighborhood will flood.

In its October 8 update , NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center said El Niño continues to strengthen, with a greater than 83% chance of strong-to-very-strong conditions through January–March 2027 . The agency also said the chances remain high for an event that could exceed the strength of previous El Niño episodes dating back to 1950. That remains a forecast, rather than a record already established. A potentially historic event makes preparation worthwhile; it does not guarantee historic weather in every state.

What El Niño could mean for your winter and what to do now

El Niño is a recurring climate pattern involving unusually warm water in the tropical Pacific and associated changes in atmospheric circulation. Its influence can shift the odds of seasonal temperature and precipitation patterns far beyond the ocean. NOAA cautions that even a powerful event does not guarantee the familiar El Niño effects everywhere.

For drivers, the most useful preparation is a plan for bad conditions. Before a winter trip, the National Weather Service recommends checking the vehicle’s lights, heater, windshield wipers and fluid levels . Carry blankets, water, nonperishable food, a flashlight and a phone charger. Check your state’s road conditions before leaving, and let someone know your route and expected arrival time. A broad outlook should not replace the forecast along your actual journey.

For households, prepare for the disruption a single storm can cause. Keep essential prescriptions, food, water, batteries and supplies for children and pets available. Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, and make sure everyone knows how to receive emergency information if the power goes out. The National Weather Service also warns that generators must never be operated in enclosed spaces.

In areas expecting more rain, flooded roads deserve particular attention. Water can hide damaged pavement, and its force is easy to underestimate. The National Weather Service says just 12 inches of rushing water can carry away most cars. Never drive around flood barriers or attempt to cross a flooded road because another vehicle made it through. Turn around and find a safe alternative.

The snowfall question remains more complicated than “wet” or “warm.” NOAA’s outlook discussed here does not provide a snowfall total for New York City, Chicago or Boston. More precipitation does not automatically mean more snow, and a warmer seasonal average does not describe every cold spell. City-specific snowfall estimates from private forecasters should be identified as their projections, rather than attributed to NOAA.

articles.title: Pentagon announces public livestream for execution of Fort Hood mass shooter
articles.standfirst: Pete Hegseth says the public will be able to watch Nidal Hasan’s firing squad execution, scheduled for December 3.
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth says the public will be able to watch Nidal Hasan’s firing squad execution, scheduled for December 3.
articles.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Thursday that the public will be able to watch the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan , a former Army officer convicted of the mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas .

In an interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln with conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice, Hegseth said Hasan “going to get a firing squad of soldiers, and we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it.”

“People need to understand that there are serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said, calling the execution method a “no-brainer.”

According to Hegseth , the execution will take place at 1 p.m. on December 3 at Fort Hood, on the same day of the week and at the same time of day as Hasan’s attack.

A Defense Department official said the execution will be livestreamed, although it remains unclear which platform will carry it.

An execution method not used in decades

The last military execution took place in 1961 , when Army Private John Bennett was hanged after being convicted of raping and attempting to murder an 11-year-old girl in Austria .

The last firing squad execution carried out by the U.S. military was that of Private Eddie Slovik in 1945 , after a court-martial convicted him of desertion during World War II .

Hasan, a former Army major and psychiatrist, opened fire at Fort Hood on November 5, 2009 , killing 13 people and wounding 32 others while shouting “Allahu akbar,” which means “ God is great” in Arabic . He was convicted of premeditated murder in 2013 through the military justice system and sentenced to death. He is currently on military death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

Hasan was paralyzed from the waist down after being shot during the attack. He later told a panel of military mental health professionals that he wished he had been killed because it would have made him a martyr for his cause. He also said that if he were executed, he would still be considered a martyr.

NBC News reported this week that the idea of using a firing squad began taking shape inside the Pentagon earlier this year, according to two U.S. officials familiar with the planning. Sean Parnell , the Pentagon’s chief spokesperson, said on social media that President Donald Trump recently approved Hegseth’s recommendation to carry out the execution.

During the interview, Hegseth was asked whether he knew if Hasan had contacted Trump or made any final requests.

“Don’t care,” Hegseth said. “We’ll see him on Dec. 3rd.”

According to the Death Penalty Information Center , once a president approves a death sentence handed down by a military court, the service member can seek habeas corpus relief through the federal court system.

If that petition is denied, the service member would be escorted from death row to the execution chamber at the United States Disciplinary Barracks. Traditionally, the prisoner would be strapped to a gurney and executed by lethal injection. However, the Defense Department has said Hasan will be executed by firing squad.

Hasan has represented himself throughout the lengthy legal process, although two attorneys from the U.S. Army Trial Defense Service have assisted him as needed. It remains unclear whether he will appeal the method of execution.

articles.title: Who is eligible to get their benefits adjusted for next year with the COLA Increase 2027?
articles.standfirst: Millions of Americans could receive higher monthly payments in 2027 as Social Security prepares to announce its annual inflation adjustment
articles.summary: Millions of Americans could receive higher monthly payments in 2027 as Social Security prepares to announce its annual inflation adjustment
articles.body:
Millions of Americans who rely on government benefits are preparing for the next annual cost-of-living adjustment, commonly known as COLA .

The increase is designed to help Social Security recipients maintain some of their purchasing power as prices for everyday necessities, including food, housing and healthcare, rise.

The adjustment is not limited to people who have retired. It also applies to eligible beneficiaries receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) , survivor benefits and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) .

The amount each person receives will depend on their existing benefit and the rules governing their particular program.

As of October 9, 2026, the Social Security Administration (SSA) has not confirmed the final COLA for 2027. The Senior Citizens League, an advocacy organization that tracks Social Security benefits, projected a 3.5% increase in September.

That would be higher than the 2.8% adjustment that took effect in 2026, although the final figure depends on the relevant inflation data.

Which beneficiaries qualify for the 2027 COLA increase?

The adjustment generally applies automatically to people already receiving eligible Social Security benefits. Recipients do not need to submit a separate application simply to receive the annual COLA .

Retired workers are among the largest groups affected. Whether someone retired at full retirement age, claimed benefits early or waited beyond full retirement age, their existing Social Security retirement benefit is adjusted when a COLA is implemented.

People receiving Social Security Disability Insurance can also qualify. SSDI provides benefits to eligible workers whose qualifying disabilities prevent them from maintaining substantial employment, subject to the program's medical and work-history requirements.

The COLA adjusts eligible payments under the same annual framework used for other Social Security benefits.

Survivors may also benefit. Social Security provides payments to eligible family members of deceased workers, including qualifying widows, widowers and children. When those payments are eligible for the annual adjustment, recipients can see their monthly benefits increase as well.

Spouses and qualifying dependents receiving benefits based on another worker's earnings record may also be covered. Eligibility depends on the type of benefit being paid, rather than simply on whether someone is related to a Social Security recipient.

Supplemental Security Income is another important category. Unlike standard Social Security retirement and disability insurance, SSI is a needs-based program for people who meet its income and resource requirements and are aged 65 or older, blind or disabled.

Eligible SSI recipients also receive annual cost-of-living adjustments. Some people receive both SSI and Social Security benefits, meaning their payments may be affected through both programs.

The crucial distinction is that a COLA does not make someone newly eligible for benefits. It adjusts payments for people who already qualify under the relevant program rules.

Someone who has not yet claimed retirement benefits, for example, should not assume that the annual increase automatically creates a payment before they become eligible and apply.

When will the increase arrive, and how much could recipients receive?

The SSA is expected to announce the official 2027 COLA on October 14, following the release of September inflation data.

The calculation compares the average Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) for July, August and September 2026 with the corresponding average from the third quarter of the previous year. The formula is established by law and is intended to reflect changes in consumer prices.

If the projected 3.5% adjustment is confirmed, the increase would vary according to a recipient's current benefit. The following examples illustrate the approximate effect before deductions:

- A monthly benefit of $1,000 would increase by about $35, to $1,035.

- A monthly benefit of $1,500 would increase by about $52.50, to $1,552.50.

- A monthly benefit of $2,000 would increase by about $70, to $2,070.

- A monthly benefit of $2,500 would increase by about $87.50, to $2,587.50.

These are estimates rather than guaranteed payment amounts. The SSA's calculation and rounding rules can cause the final figure to differ slightly, and deductions such as Medicare premiums may affect how much money a beneficiary actually receives.

For most Social Security beneficiaries, the new rates would apply to benefits payable in January 2027.

SSI recipients generally receive their adjusted amount earlier because of the payment calendar: the January 2027 SSI payment is scheduled to arrive on December 31, 2026, since January 1 is a federal holiday.

It is important to remember that a larger monthly payment does not necessarily mean a recipient's spending power will increase by the same amount.

If rent, groceries, utilities and medical expenses rise faster than the adjustment, household budgets may remain under pressure.

How can beneficiaries check their adjusted payments?

Once the SSA finalizes the COLA , beneficiaries can check official notices to learn how their individual payments will change.

People with a my Social Security account can use the online service to access benefit information and, where available, receive their COLA notice electronically.

Recipients should rely on official SSA communications rather than unofficial estimates when planning their finances.

People who receive SSI should also remember that their eligibility and payment amounts remain subject to the program's income and resource rules. A COLA changes benefit rates, but it does not remove those requirements.

For anyone who is not yet receiving benefits, the annual adjustment is not a substitute for checking eligibility or filing a claim. Retirement, disability, survivor and SSI programs have different qualification criteria, and the SSA provides separate guidance for each.

The bottom line is that the 2027 COLA is expected to help eligible retirees, disabled workers, survivors and SSI recipients receive higher payments next year.

The projected 3.5% increase offers an early indication of what beneficiaries might expect, but the official rate is still pending. Recipients should look for the SSA's October announcement and review their individual notices before treating any forecast as a confirmed change to their income.

articles.title: How is the COLA Increase calculated each year, and what is being considered for the 2027 adjustment?
articles.standfirst: Social Security beneficiaries are awaiting the next annual cost-of-living adjustment, with an early forecast pointing to a 3.5% increase in 2027
articles.summary: Social Security beneficiaries are awaiting the next annual cost-of-living adjustment, with an early forecast pointing to a 3.5% increase in 2027
articles.body:
The annual Social Security cost-of-living adjustment, better known as COLA , is designed to help benefits keep pace with rising prices.

For millions of retired Americans , people with disabilities and eligible survivors, the increase can make a difference to household budgets as the costs of groceries, housing, utilities and healthcare continue to change.

Unlike an increase negotiated by lawmakers, the regular COLA is determined through a formula established by law. The Social Security Administration (SSA) uses a particular measure of consumer inflation to calculate whether benefits should rise and, if so, by how much.

For 2027, The Senior Citizens League and other inflation trackers have pointed to a potential increase of around 3.5%. That remains a projection rather than a confirmed benefit adjustment as of October 9, 2026.

The SSA is expected to announce the official figure on October 14, after the release of September's inflation data.

The final percentage will matter to people receiving retirement benefits, Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and survivor payments. Eligible Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients will also see their payments adjusted.

However, the increase will not be identical in dollar terms for every beneficiary because it is calculated from existing benefit amounts.

How the government calculates the annual COLA

The calculation is based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, commonly called the CPI-W. Published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, this index tracks changes in the prices paid for a range of goods and services.

The SSA compares the average CPI-W for July, August and September of the current year with the average for the same three months in the last year a COLA was determined. If the latest third-quarter average is higher, the percentage increase becomes the basis for the adjustment.

The result is rounded to the nearest tenth of a percentage point under the established formula.

This means the government does not simply look at one month's inflation report or use the annual inflation rate quoted in the news. The specific CPI-W figures from the third quarter determine the outcome.

For the 2027 adjustment, the relevant comparison is between the average CPI-W for July through September 2026 and the corresponding period in 2025. July and August figures are already available, but the September data are needed to complete the calculation.

An inflation forecast can provide an indication of the likely result, but it cannot replace the final published figures. A higher-than-expected September reading could affect the estimate, while a lower reading could change it in the other direction.

The method has been used for Social Security COLAs since 1975, when automatic annual adjustments were introduced.

The system was designed to reduce the need for separate congressional action each time inflation affected the purchasing power of benefits.

What is being forecast for the 2027 adjustment?

The Senior Citizens League has estimated that the 2027 COLA could reach 3.5%. That would be a larger increase than the 2.8% adjustment applied in 2026 and the 2.5% increase in 2025.

However, the estimate remains provisional until the SSA completes its calculation and publishes the official rate.

If a 3.5% increase is confirmed, the approximate effect on monthly benefits before deductions would look like this:

- A person receiving $1,000 a month would gain about $35, bringing the payment to $1,035.

- Someone receiving $1,500 would receive approximately $52.50 more, for a new total of $1,552.50.

- A beneficiary currently receiving $2,000 would gain around $70, bringing the payment to $2,070.

- A monthly benefit of $2,500 would rise by approximately $87.50, to $2,587.50.

These examples illustrate the effect of the projected rate; they are not official payment calculations. The actual dollar increase depends on the recipient's benefit and the SSA's calculation and rounding rules.

Medicare premiums and other deductions can also affect the amount ultimately deposited into a person's account.

Under the usual schedule, the 2027 COLA will apply to Social Security benefits payable in January 2027. SSI recipients generally receive their adjusted January payment on December 31, 2026, because January 1 is a federal holiday.

The increase is intended to offset some of the effects of inflation, but it does not guarantee that recipients will be able to afford every expense more easily.

If rent, insurance, food or medical costs rise faster than the COLA , beneficiaries may still feel financial pressure even after their payments increase.

Could the COLA formula itself change?

Although the 2027 adjustment is expected to be calculated under the existing CPI-W rules, policymakers have considered alternative ways to measure inflation for Social Security purposes.

One longstanding proposal is to use the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly, or CPI-E. This index is designed to reflect spending patterns among older Americans, who may devote a larger share of their budgets to healthcare and certain other costs than the population represented by the CPI-W.

Supporters argue that an elderly-focused measure could better reflect the inflation experienced by retirees.

However, adopting it would require a change to the current system; it is not the formula used to determine the 2027 COLA under existing law.

Other proposals have considered using a chained version of the CPI-W, which accounts for how consumers change their spending when prices shift.

The Social Security Administration 's Office of the Chief Actuary estimates that this alternative could reduce annual COLAs by approximately 0.3 percentage points on average. It remains a policy proposal rather than an automatic change to the current calculation.

These debates reflect a wider disagreement over how Social Security should balance the purchasing power of benefits against the programme's long-term finances.

A measure that produces larger annual adjustments could provide more protection against rising expenses for some beneficiaries, while a formula producing smaller increases could reduce projected programme costs.

For now, beneficiaries should distinguish between proposals being discussed and the calculation that will actually determine their 2027 payments. The CPI-W remains the measure used under current law, and the final third-quarter figures will establish the next adjustment.

What beneficiaries should watch next

The most important date is October 14, 2026, when the September inflation report is due and the SSA is expected to announce the 2027 COLA. Beneficiaries can then use the official rate to estimate their new monthly payments and look for their individual notices from Social Security.

Recipients can access benefit information through their my Social Security accounts, while the SSA's website provides official announcements and guidance on how COLAs affect different programmes.

The projected 3.5% increase would offer some additional income to eligible recipients, but it should not be treated as guaranteed until the official announcement.

The precise amount will depend on the completed inflation calculation, and a higher monthly payment may still leave households managing difficult choices as living costs rise.

Ultimately, the COLA is a mechanism for adjusting Social Security payments in response to measured inflation.

Understanding the CPI-W formula, the timing of the annual announcement and the difference between forecasts and confirmed policy can help beneficiaries prepare for 2027 without relying on estimates that may change.

articles.title: Who was John Bennett? The last soldier executed in the United States 65 years ago
articles.standfirst: Army Private John Bennett was hanged at Fort Leavenworth's military prison in Kansas after being convicted of rape
articles.summary: Army Private John Bennett was hanged at Fort Leavenworth's military prison in Kansas after being convicted of rape
articles.body:
Capital punishment within the U.S. military has a long and complex history, historically reserved for severe offenses such as murder, treason, and rape during times of war or active service.

Throughout the twentieth century, military executions carried out by the armed forces were subject to intense scrutiny, particularly regarding how capital punishment was administered across different racial groups .

While the ultimate penalty was theoretically designed to maintain military discipline and punish the most heinous crimes, historical data and legal reviews have repeatedly highlighted deep systemic disparities in how these death sentences were handed down and enforced.

The Tragic Case of Private John Bennett

Marking a sobering milestone in American jurisprudence, it has now been exactly 65 years since the U.S. military last carried out a death sentence on a service member. On April 13, 1961 , Army Pvt. John Bennett was hanged at the military prison at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, after being convicted of raping and attempting to kill an 11-year-old Austrian girl .

At 26 years old , Bennett’s execution generated very little media fanfare at the time, but looking back through a modern lens, the case exposes glaring racial inequalities and legal shortcomings.

Bennett was an African-American soldier , the victim was white, and his legal representation during the trial was described by historians as brief and ineffective.

Legal experts have noted that during the six-year span between Bennett’s conviction and his eventual execution, eight other Black soldiers faced the death penalty, while six white prisoners on military death row managed to escape execution, with President Dwight Eisenhower commuting four of those sentences and the court sparing two.

Furthermore, historical archives and legal reviews reveal that Bennett suffered from underlying mental health problems that likely would have spared him under contemporary standards of justice, yet his defense counsel never introduced his psychological background during the trial.

Legal scholars, such as Yale Law School professor Eugene R. Fidell , have long pointed out that the military death penalty disproportionately targeted African-American service members.

Statistics compiled by legal experts show that during World War II , when Black troops accounted for less than 10% of the total Army, 55 out of the 70 soldiers executed in Europe were Black .

Following President Harry Truman ’s 1948 order desegregating the armed forces, that racial disparity actually widened; between 1954 and 1961 , 11 of the 12 service members executed by the military were African-American .

A comprehensive 2012 study analyzing military capital cases between 1984 and 2005 further confirmed that minority defendants were twice as likely to receive the death penalty as white defendants, a disproportionate rate significantly higher than that found in civilian courts.

As the decades have passed since John Bennett walked to the gallows in the Fort Leavenworth boiler room, federal and military systems have largely moved away from capital punishment, leaving his execution as a dark and defining final chapter in the history of American military capital punishment.

articles.title: Christa Pike wins her first legal battle as she is already talking and walking following a miraculous recovery
articles.standfirst: The state of Tennessee failed to successfully execute Pike on September 30.
articles.summary: The state of Tennessee failed to successfully execute Pike on September 30.
articles.body:
C hrista Pike has won a fresh opportunity to challenge her death sentence after a Tennessee judge reopened her lawsuit against the state's lethal injection procedure, following an execution attempt on September 30 that failed to kill her. The ruling allows her attorneys to continue fighting against another attempt, raising questions about how Tennessee will proceed as Governor Bill Lee has suspended executions through the end of 2026 and ordered an independent investigation.

Pike had spent around three decades on death row for the murder of the 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer and was scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Her attorneys said execution personnel administered two doses of pentobarbital and used at least seven needles while attempting to establish intravenous access. One needle reportedly emerged from her arm bent at a right angle. Pike 's lawyer said she later developed pneumonia and a blood clot in her arm and was unable to eat. Reports that she has since regained the ability to walk and talk have drawn further attention to her recovery. Pike had challenged Tennessee 's lethal injection protocol in January, arguing that the single-drug method violated constitutional protections against cruel and unusual punishment. Her lawyers cited concerns about inadequate training, secrecy and the difficulty of accessing her veins, but the Tennessee Supreme Court dismissed the complaint in May. However, on October 8 , Judge I'Ashea Myles reopened the case in Nashville , finding that Pike had demonstrated "extreme, unique, exceptional, or extraordinary circumstances”.

What comes next for Christa Pike?

The ruling does not overturn Pike 's death sentence or automatically prevent another execution attempt. It gives her attorneys another opportunity to challenge the procedure's constitutionality. During the Thursday hearing, Tennessee ’s Assistant Attorney General William Ayers could not tell the judge whether officials would schedule another execution, but no new date has been announced. Whilst the defense attorney Stephen Ross Johnson has warned that another attempt could face substantial legal obstacles. Alternative methods, including electrocution or hanging, would raise separate legal questions. Pike 's attorneys are seeking to have her sentence commuted to life imprisonment, although the outcome remains uncertain, and the United States Supreme Court has historically declined to impose a blanket prohibition on second execution attempts. Slemmer ’s mother, May Martinez , attended the execution and later described the experience as a "mess", adding she feels is owed an apology by Tennessee . Pike 's legal challenge will now proceed, but whether it will prevent another execution attempt or change her sentence remains unresolved.

articles.title: Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay brings Trump into her celebration with an unexpected joke
articles.standfirst: The South African jurist drew laughter with a remark about the president, who has repeatedly said he deserves the prize
articles.summary: The South African jurist drew laughter with a remark about the president, who has repeatedly said he deserves the prize
articles.body:
Navi Pillay had just learned she had won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize when she brought Donald Trump into the celebration. As colleagues applauded her at a legal conference in Nuremberg, Germany, on October 9, she joked: “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.” The room erupted in laughter. The award ceremony will take place on December 10 at Oslo City Hall in Norway.

The joke touched on Trump’s well-known desire to win the Nobel . It also appeared to reference last year’s winner, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, who gave him her medal in January.

Trump’s Nobel Peace Prize push ends with a joke at his expense

Trump has repeatedly argued that his diplomatic efforts deserve the award. On October 7, he again claimed credit for resolving eight conflicts, although some parties dispute his role and fighting has resumed in several places. His pursuit also comes amid the continuing conflict with Iran following U.S.-Israeli strikes, while peace in Ukraine remains elusive.

The leaders of Israel, Cambodia and Pakistan publicly said they had nominated Trump. However, the Nobel Committee has not confirmed his nomination or whether he was shortlisted, as nomination records remain confidential for 50 years.

Trump has received a separate peace award. FIFA president Gianni Infantino presented him with the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize on December 5, 2025, during the 2026 World Cup draw in Washington. The soccer organization said it recognized his efforts to promote peace.

Who is Navi Pillay, the Nobel Peace Prize winner?

Pillay, 85, is a South African jurist and former U.N. human rights chief whose career began fighting apartheid and continued in international courts.

The Nobel Committee recognized her work promoting peace through international law, including efforts to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. She currently serves as an ad hoc judge in the International Court of Justice case concerning allegations of genocide against the Rohingya in Myanmar.

There was no publicly announced shortlist. Among the potential winners highlighted by the independent Peace Research Institute Oslo were Mykola Kuleba, founder of Save Ukraine; Save the Children; Sudan’s volunteer Emergency Response Rooms; the Committee to Protect Journalists; the International Court of Justice; the International Criminal Court; and the International Space Station partnership. These were expert picks, not confirmed finalists.

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias Will Make Landfall Tonight: Everything You Need to Know
articles.standfirst: Florida.
articles.summary: Florida.
articles.body:
Category 3 Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall in northwestern Florida this Friday, October 9, near Pensacola and Navarre Beach, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC) .

What time will Hurricane Isaias reach Florida?

The storm is expected to make landfall between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. Central Time. However, the exact timing could change as the system moves forward.

The area facing the greatest threat is the Panhandle, in the northwestern part of the state. In response to the risk, Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in 25 counties to facilitate emergency response efforts .

How will Hurricane Isaias affect Florida?

One of the main dangers is storm surge, which could raise water levels by 7 to 10 feet . This increases the risk of coastal flooding, road disruptions and damage to homes near the coast.

Strong winds are another concern. Isaias is expected to make landfall with maximum sustained winds of 115 to 120 mph .

Power outages are also among the potential consequences of the storm. As part of the preparations, more than 5,000 members of the Florida National Guard have been deployed to support emergency response efforts, while utility crews are preparing to address potential damage to the power grid.

Safety recommendations for residents

People living in threatened areas should monitor weather alerts and follow instructions from local authorities. Once severe conditions begin, the safest option is to shelter in place and avoid going outside while the hurricane passes .

articles.title: Winter is arriving early: first widespread snowfall could bring a foot of snow to the Rockies
articles.standfirst: Some locations could receive 6 to 12 inches of snow between Saturday and Monday
articles.summary: Some locations could receive 6 to 12 inches of snow between Saturday and Monday
articles.body:
A hurricane's remnants, plunging temperatures and a major shift in the jet stream are combining to produce an unusual early-season weather event across the western United States : the first widespread snowfall of the season is forecast for the Northern Rockies, with some mountainous areas potentially receiving a foot of snow.

While the Southeast prepares for the impacts of Hurricane Isaias and its remnants over the weekend of October 10, parts of Idaho, Montana and Wyoming are bracing for a very different threat. The approaching storm could bring accumulating snow to elevations as low as 4,000 feet, potentially delivering the first snowfall of the season to some valleys while burying higher terrain.

"The first widespread snowfall of the season is expected across the Northern Rockies this weekend into early next week," the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Weather Prediction Center said in an October 7 post on X.

AccuWeather senior meteorologist Brett Anderson forecast that some locations could receive 6 to 12 inches of snow between Saturday, October 10, and Monday, October 12. The highest elevations could see even greater accumulations. The forecast stands out not only because of the timing but also because of the unusual combination of weather systems expected to produce the snow.

Why is this October snowfall so unusual?

Snow in the Northern Rockies during October is not unprecedented. Mountain peaks can receive snow well before winter officially arrives, and some high-elevation areas had already experienced snowfall in recent weeks. What makes this forecast unusual is the potential for widespread accumulation at lower elevations, combined with the role of moisture from a tropical system in fueling the storm.

"While there has been some high-elevation snow in recent weeks in the Cascades and northern Rockies, snow levels will dip much lower in portions of Idaho, Montana and Wyoming," AccuWeather senior meteorologist Adam Douty said.

Some valley locations could experience their first snowfall of the season, while heavier accumulations are expected across higher terrain. T he National Weather Service office in Missoula, Montana, highlighted the unusual source of the incoming moisture in its forecast discussion.

"This is a very rare circumstance, but moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Rachel will track northeastwards from California and Nevada towards the Yellowstone and Wyoming area," the office said. The key is the interaction between two different atmospheric ingredients: abundant moisture associated with the remnants of a Pacific hurricane and a surge of colder air behind a strong cold front.

Tropical systems typically bring warm, moisture-rich air. When that moisture encounters sufficiently cold conditions, however, it can contribute to heavy precipitation in the form of snow, particularly across mountainous terrain.

A significant early-season snow event

In this case, a large trough of low pressure over the West is expected to help steer Rachel's remnants northeastward while ushering colder air into the Northern Rockies. The result could be a significant early-season snow event across parts of the region. Hurricane Rachel's remnants are fueling a complicated weather pattern

The storm's unusual character extends beyond snowfall. According to the Weather Prediction Center, the remnants of eastern Pacific Hurricane Rachel are expected to interact with a broad trough of low pressure, bringing widespread heavy rainfall and localized flash-flooding risks from the Southwest into the Great Basin and Rockies, with precipitation potentially extending into the northern Plains on October 11 and 12.

The cold front trailing the system is expected to lower snow levels, allowing accumulating snow to develop at higher elevations across the Northern Rockies. That combination presents a forecasting challenge because the same storm system can produce very different hazards depending on location and elevation. Lower, warmer areas may experience heavy rain, while higher and colder terrain receives accumulating snow.

The amount of snowfall will depend on the storm's precise track, the temperature profile of the atmosphere and how much moisture reaches the region as colder air moves in. Although a foot of snow is possible in some of the highest elevations, accumulations will vary considerably across the affected areas.

articles.title: How much are Disability Benefits increasing with the last COLA 2027 projection?
articles.standfirst: The Cost-of-Living Adjustment was set at 2.8% for 2026
articles.summary: The Cost-of-Living Adjustment was set at 2.8% for 2026
articles.body:
Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) recipients could see their monthly payments increase in 2027, with the latest Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) forecasts pointing to a rise of between 3.4% and 3.6%.

A 3.6% increase, as projected by AARP, would give beneficiaries a larger monthly payment to help manage rising prices. However, the official figure won't be confirmed until October 14, when the Social Security Administration releases its annual adjustment.

The final increase will depend on inflation data, with the adjustment applying to Social Security retirement, disability and survivor benefits and the projection is higher than the 2.8% COLA implemented in 2026, which increased payments by an average of approximately $56 per month for retired workers.

A similar increase in disability benefits would depend on each recipient's existing monthly payment. For example, a person receiving $1000 per month in SSDI could receive an additional $36 under a 3.6% adjustment.

That would bring the monthly benefit to $1036. Someone receiving $1500 would gain $54 per month, while a beneficiary collecting $2000 would receive an extra $72.

Once announced, the 2027 COLA will apply to eligible SSDI beneficiaries, helping their payments keep pace with inflation. The higher benefits are scheduled to begin in January 2027, although the first payment is due on December 31, because New Year's Day is a federal holiday.

Why retirees should be wary of COLA increases

The Senior Citizens League has projected a 3.5% increase, while independent analyst Mary Johnson estimates the adjustment could reach 3.4%. These remain forecasts rather than confirmed payment changes, and the final COLA could differ.

But a higher COLA doesn't necessarily translate into an equivalent improvement in recipients' finances.

Medicare premiums can reduce the amount beneficiaries have left to spend, particularly for those enrolled in Medicare Part B or subject to income-related monthly adjustment amounts (IRMAA).

Taxes may also affect some recipients, depending on their overall income and filing status. Social Security benefits can be taxable for people whose combined income exceeds applicable thresholds, meaning an increase could have consequences beyond the monthly payment itself.

Disability beneficiaries should therefore distinguish between the projected percentage increase and the amount they will actually receive after applicable deductions.

Until the Social Security Administration announces the official 2027 COLA, the 3.4% to 3.6% range remains an estimate, not a guaranteed increase. The adjustment is calculated using the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W).

The Social Security Administration compares average inflation readings from the third quarter of the current year with those from the same period in the previous year to determine the annual percentage increase.

articles.title: Who is Katie Zacharia? The new White House press secretary replacing Karoline Leavitt
articles.standfirst: The new White House press secretary has worked in conservative media, political advocacy and Homeland Security
articles.summary: The new White House press secretary has worked in conservative media, political advocacy and Homeland Security
articles.body:
The White House briefing room is preparing for a new spokesperson after President Donald Trump announced Friday that Katie Zacharia would succeed Karoline Leavitt , who left the administration in August.

Zacharia 's appointment ends a six-week vacancy in one of Washington's most visible positions, placing a longtime Trump supporter in charge of communicating the administration's policies and responding to questions from the national press.

Trump announced his decision on Truth Social, describing Zacharia as “a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning,” while highlighting her involvement in his previous presidential campaigns.

The selection brings someone already familiar with conservative media into a position that requires regular interaction with reporters from across the political spectrum.

Zacharia , 41, is a California-based attorney, political commentator and mother of four whose career has included work in conservative organizations, government communications and television.

She earned both her undergraduate degree and law degree from Pepperdine University before establishing a career that combined legal work with political advocacy and public affairs.

Her previous positions include serving as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative nonprofit founded by Trump ally Richard Grenell , and working with the anti-abortion organization White Rose Resistance.

Earlier in 2026, Zacharia briefly served as a spokesperson at the Department of Homeland Security before joining Trump Media & Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social.

She has also appeared regularly on Fox News and Newsmax, discussing political developments and offering commentary from a conservative perspective.

Why did Karoline Leavitt leave the White House?

Leavitt announced her departure on August 12 and officially stepped down on August 27, explaining that she wanted to spend more time with her young children.

She had served as Trump 's press secretary since January 2025, following her role as national press secretary during his successful 2024 presidential campaign.

Leavitt became known for her confrontational exchanges with reporters and frequent defense of the president's policies, establishing a recognizable presence at White House briefings.

Her next position will be outside government, with Fox News announcing that she will join the network as an on-air contributor beginning November 1.

Zacharia faces immediate challenge in Washington

The incoming press secretary takes over ahead of November's midterm elections, with the administration facing questions about its policies and legal challenges involving restrictions on media access.

Zacharia acknowledged the responsibility in a statement following her appointment, thanking Trump and describing the opportunity as the “honor of a lifetime.”

“The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day,” she wrote on X.

Her appointment signals continuity in Trump 's preference for politically aligned communications officials, although her effectiveness in the briefing room will depend on how she handles scrutiny from reporters.

articles.standfirst: The drawing is scheduled for 23:00 ET/20:00 PT.
articles.summary: The drawing is scheduled for 23:00 ET/20:00 PT.
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $516 million ahead of Saturday's October 10 drawing, giving players another opportunity to compete for one of the biggest lottery prizes currently available in the United States.

The winning numbers haven't yet been announced. The drawing is scheduled for 23:00 ET/20:00 PT on Saturday, with the jackpot's cash option estimated at $212.6 million before taxes.

The previous drawing, held on Wednesday, October 7, ended without a jackpot winner. The numbers drawn were 11, 13, 14, 21 and 65, with 19 selected as the red Powerball . The Power Play multiplier was 2X.

Saturday's drawing will determine whether a ticket matches all six numbers or the jackpot rolls over again. The official results and prize information will be available after the drawing takes place.

Players should check the official results after the 11 p.m. ET drawing. The advertised jackpot is $516 million, while the estimated lump-sum cash payment stands at $212.6 million.

Winners who choose the annuity option receive the advertised prize through a series of payments over time, while the cash option provides a smaller one-time payment before taxes.

Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Tickets cost $2, and players select five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26.

How to check Powerball results and claim prizes

The odds of winning the jackpot are 1 in 292.2 million. Players can also win smaller prizes by matching some of the numbers drawn, even if they do not secure the top prize.

The optional Power Play feature costs an additional $1 per ticket and can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes. The multiplier drawn does not increase the jackpot itself.

Powerball is played across 45 states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Ticket availability, purchase deadlines and prize-claim procedures depend on the jurisdiction where a ticket is sold.

Players can check the official Powerball website or their state lottery's results page after the drawing to confirm the numbers and review the prize breakdown. A ticket should be checked carefully against all six numbers, along with any applicable Power Play selection.

The jackpot has grown through successive drawings without a top-prize winner, reaching $516 million for October 10. Whether Saturday's drawing produces a jackpot winner or another rollover will only be known once the official results are released.

articles.title: From brain death to back in a cell: Christa Pike's shocking return to prison leaves Tennessee in uncharted legal waters
articles.standfirst: Pike has been in prison since 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer
articles.summary: Pike has been in prison since 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer
articles.body:
Christa Pike has returned to prison after being discharged from hospital following Tennessee 's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection, leaving the state facing difficult questions about the future of her death sentence. The 50-year-old inmate was transferred back to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville on Saturday, October 10, her attorneys confirmed. She remains under medical care as she recovers from the September 30 execution attempt.

In a statement, Pike 's legal team said she was grateful to the first responders and medical professionals who treated her. Her attorneys added that they would continue monitoring her recovery. Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital, the drug Tennessee uses for lethal injections. Instead of dying as intended, she was taken to hospital in critical condition, where she spent several days unconscious and required a ventilator before regaining consciousness. The failed procedure has intensified scrutiny of the state's execution practices. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has suspended executions for the remainder of 2026 while an independent review examines what went wrong. The state's corrections commissioner, Frank Strada , also resigned following the incident. Pike 's return to prison does not resolve the legal questions surrounding her sentence. A judge has ordered Tennessee officials to preserve evidence connected to the execution attempt, including medical equipment, records and recordings, as her attorneys seek answers about how the procedure failed. Her lawyers have also challenged the constitutionality of subjecting her to another execution attempt after what happened. Whether Tennessee will seek to carry out her sentence again remains uncertain.

How did Pike kill Colleen Slemmer?

Pike was sentenced to death for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in January 1995, a fellow student at a Job Corps training program in Knoxville, Tennessee after believing Colleen was interested in her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp . The pair, and their acquaintance Shadolla Peterson , lured Slemmer to an isolated wooded area near the University of Tennessee campus under the pretense of making peace. According to court testimony, Pike and Shipp attacked Slemmer while Peterson acted as a lookout. The assault lasted approximately 30 minutes and involved repeated beatings and cutting. Shipp carved a pentagram into Slemmer 's chest, whilst Pike used a meat cleaver before repeatedly striking the victim's head with a piece of asphalt, causing fatal brain injuries. Pike was arrested within days and subsequently convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder. On March 30, 1996, she received a death sentence for the killing and a 25-year prison term for the conspiracy charge. Appeals did not overturn the sentence, and Pike remained on death row for three decades before Tennessee scheduled her execution for September 30 and now, her survival has created an extraordinary legal predicament for state officials.

A judge has ordered Tennessee officials to preserve evidence connected to the execution attempt, including medical equipment, records and recordings, as her attorneys seek answers about how the procedure failed. Her lawyers have also challenged the constitutionality of subjecting her to another execution attempt after what happened. Whether Tennessee will seek to carry out her sentence again remains uncertain.
How did Pike kill Colleen Slemmer?

Pike was sentenced to death for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in January 1995, a fellow student at a Job Corps training program in Knoxville, Tennessee after believing Colleen was interested in her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp . The pair, and their acquaintance Shadolla Peterson , lured Slemmer to an isolated wooded area near the University of Tennessee campus under the pretense of making peace. According to court testimony, Pike and Shipp attacked Slemmer while Peterson acted as a lookout. The assault lasted approximately 30 minutes and involved repeated beatings and cutting. Shipp carved a pentagram into Slemmer 's chest, whilst Pike used a meat cleaver before repeatedly striking the victim's head with a piece of asphalt, causing fatal brain injuries. Pike was arrested within days and subsequently convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder. On March 30, 1996, she received a death sentence for the killing and a 25-year prison term for the conspiracy charge. Appeals did not overturn the sentence, and Pike remained on death row for three decades before Tennessee scheduled her execution for September 30 and now, her survival has created an extraordinary legal predicament for state officials.

articles.title: Trump erupts after missing out on the Nobel Peace Prize: “I have resolved eight wars and nobody knows who the winner is”
articles.standfirst: The American leader points to the winner, the South African jurist Navanethem Pillay
articles.summary: The American leader points to the winner, the South African jurist Navanethem Pillay
articles.body:
Donald Trump has once again lashed out at the Norwegian Nobel Committee after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African jurist Navanethem Pillay . The President of the United States questioned the choice of the award and said that most people do not even know who the winner is.

“This is the woman who has received the Nobel Peace Prize over the United States and whose representative, me, has resolved eight wars. I know nothing about this woman, and neither does anyone else” , Trump wrote in a lengthy post on his social media. In addition, he accused Pillay of being anti-Israel and once again claimed credit for his role in several international conflicts.

The president went a step further and claimed that, for the merits he attributes to himself in foreign policy, he should have received the prize on multiple occasions. “I have resolved eight wars. I should have won eight Nobel Prizes” , he stated.

Trump boasts of his international achievements

In his message, the Republican leader went over a long list of actions he considers successes of his administration . Among them, he highlighted alleged advances in the Middle East, his role in international conflicts and various diplomatic actions that, according to his version, prevented the outbreak of new wars.

Trump also recalled the support he has received in the past from Venezuelan opposition figure María Corina Machado , whom he cited as one of the voices who have publicly argued that he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize.

The U.S. president even went so far as to claim that he has “saved more lives than anyone in history,” while also taking credit for the release of Israeli hostages, progress against Nicolás Maduro’s Venezuelan regime, and the weakening of Iran’s military capabilities.

He also argued that his diplomacy has helped ease tensions between the two Koreas and in the Asia-Pacific region, in addition to highlighting the increase in military spending by NATO countries to 5% of GDP.

articles.title: How much is the Social Security Income increasing with the latest COLA projection for 2027?
articles.standfirst: Social Security is set to increase once again in 2027 as inflation continues to rise
articles.summary: Social Security is set to increase once again in 2027 as inflation continues to rise
articles.body:
Millions of Americans could see a larger Social Security payment in 2027 if the latest inflation forecast holds as The Senior Citizens League (TSCL) estimates that the next Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) could reach 3.5%. Potentially delivering a bigger raise than beneficiaries received this year, the projection remains an estimate rather than a confirmed increase and the Social Security Administration (SSA) determines the annual adjustment using inflation data.

The official announcement expected in October, and the new rate is then applied to eligible benefits beginning in January 2027, with predictions representing a more substantial boost, although its actual value would depend on how much each recipient currently receives. So how could a 3.5% rise look once it affects Social Security payments? Consider someone whose monthly benefit is $2,000. If the projected rate becomes official, their payment will rise by $70 to $2,070 per month, a recipient receiving $2,500 would gain $87.50 monthly, taking their benefit to $2,587.50. These examples illustrate what the forecast could mean for household budgets; they are not confirmed benefit amounts for 2027. The final adjustment will be determined by the SSA 's official calculation.

How is Social Security funded in the United States?

Social Security relies mainly on taxes collected from workers' earnings as employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages, with employers paying an equal share. Self-employed Americans typically cover both portions. There is a limit on how much annual income is subject to Social Security tax, though and for 2026, that threshold stands at $184,500. Earnings above it are exempt from the Social Security portion of payroll taxes, although Medicare taxes generally continue to apply. Rather than placing each worker's contributions into a personal account, the system uses most incoming tax revenue to finance benefits being paid now. Its two principal trust funds serve different groups: Old-Age and Survivors Insurance covers eligible retirees and surviving family members, while Disability Insurance supports qualifying disabled workers and their dependents. Additional revenue comes from federal income taxes on some Social Security benefits and interest earned on trust fund reserves invested in US government securities so that when incoming money falls short of scheduled payments, the reserves can help cover the difference. Long-term funding remains a concern as the population ages and the balance between contributing workers and beneficiaries changes. According to the 2026 Trustees Report , the retirement and survivor trust fund is projected to pay scheduled benefits in full until the fourth quarter of 2032. Without legislative action, ongoing income would then cover an estimated 78% of scheduled benefits so whilst a higher COLA would increase monthly payments, but it would not resolve Social Security 's longer-term funding pressures.

articles.title: Who is the Erie shooter? What is known so far about the death of 9 people in Pennsylvania
articles.standfirst: The Police have not shared the identity of the father of the family, who also died, for now
articles.summary: The Police have not shared the identity of the father of the family, who also died, for now
articles.body:
A shooting in a residential area of a city in northern Pennsylvania left nine people dead, including two children, a pregnant woman, and the suspected attacker, authorities said.

The police chief of the city of Erie, Rick Lorah, said that the attacker, a 45-year-old man, was related to seven of the victims of Friday's shooting, while the eighth was a friend of the pregnant woman.

Video and audio evidence recovered by investigators showed two “distressed” women arriving at the house shortly before 5 in the afternoon and knocking on the door, he said. The attacker then came out and shot them before going back inside.

Police arrived and found the two women dead outside. Inside they found the bodies of a 5-year-old boy, a 1-year-old girl, two more women, two young men, and the attacker.

"Lorah declined to speak about the reason, but said investigators would speak with other relatives and examine the cell phones of the women who were killed outside the home.

“They knew that something was happening in that house,” he said. “We have to find out what it is about.”

“I haven’t seen anything like it in 28 years in the Police”

Officers arrived within minutes after receiving an alert through ShotSpotter, a controversial gunshot detection system that relies on artificial intelligence and a network of microphones to identify gunfire. The city stated in a release that no additional shots were fired after that.

“The sounds heard during the police response, which could have been mistaken for gunshots, were flashbang grenades related to the tactical response of law enforcement,” the city said.

“I haven't seen anything like this in my more than 28 years (in the Police),” Lorah told a local news outlet earlier in the day. “I'm not sure the city of Erie has ever seen the loss of life and devastation that we have just witnessed.”

Governor Josh Shapiro said he offered the “full support” of his administration to Erie Mayor Daria Devlin. Erie is about 190 kilometers (120 miles) north of Pittsburgh.

articles.title: The world's most haunted road is called Clinton Road and is very close to New York: “Ghosts appeared in terrifying forms”
articles.standfirst: Americans might want to be wary when travelling through West Milford, Passaic County
articles.summary: Americans might want to be wary when travelling through West Milford, Passaic County
articles.body:
Drivers looking for a quiet route through the New Jersey countryside might want to think twice before taking a nighttime drive along Clinton Road , and the 10-mile stretch of highway has become notorious for reports of paranormal encounters. Earning the top spot in a worldwide ranking of haunted roads for the third consecutive year and located in West Milford , Passaic County , the heavily wooded road is close to New York City and has developed a reputation built on generations of local folklore.

According to a ranking published by car rental company Sixt, its unsettling atmosphere and stories of unexplained sightings have made it a destination for curious visitors and paranormal enthusiasts. The road's reputation is not new. In 1905, writer J. Percy Crayon described the surrounding area as a place where “robbers, witches and ghosts that made their appearance in frightful forms” supposedly lurked. More than a century later, Clinton Road continues to attract attention from those fascinated by the supernatural and one of the best-known stories concerns Ghost Boy , a spirit said to haunt a bridge along the road. Legend claims anyone who throws a coin into the water below will see it returned by the ghost. Visitors still reportedly leave coins in the stream near Dead Man's Curve , keeping the story alive. Clinton Road is also associated with mysterious lights that appear among the trees after dark. These so-called ghost lights are described as floating orbs or unexplained flashes that can seemingly surround drivers travelling alone along the isolated route. Other accounts involve phantom vehicles, including a black Chevrolet Camaro and an old pickup truck. In these stories, the cars appear in a driver's rearview mirror before disappearing into the darkness, leaving motorists wondering whether they witnessed something supernatural.

Where is the most haunted place in the USA?

Beyond Clinton Road , another location has earned a lasting place in the USA 's paranormal folklore as Myrtles Plantation , near St. Francisville, Louisiana , is frequently described as one of the most haunted houses in the nation. Built in 1796, the property reflects the history of the American South , including the era of slavery and its age, distinctive architecture and legends surrounding former residents have helped establish its reputation among ghost hunters and tourists interested in the unexplained. The most famous story concerns Chloe , an enslaved woman who allegedly wore a green turban to hide an injured ear and according to the legend, she poisoned a cake with oleander leaves, killing members of the Woodruff family. The story claims she was subsequently murdered by other enslaved people, and visitors have reported seeing a woman resembling her on the grounds. However, there is no reliable historical evidence confirming the tale. Another legend centers on William Winter , a plantation owner who was shot and killed in 1871 - according to local accounts, he staggered into the house after being wounded and collapsed on the staircase, with reports of footsteps and strange noises ever since.

articles.title: SNAP benefits COLA increase 2027: How much may your food stamps increase for next year?
articles.standfirst: SNAP benefits are due to rise in line with the anticipated Cost of Living Adjustment increase
articles.summary: SNAP benefits are due to rise in line with the anticipated Cost of Living Adjustment increase
articles.body:
Millions of Americans receiving food assistance are facing new benefit amounts and income eligibility limits for the upcoming fiscal year as the annual Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) are predicted to increase Social Security payments. Maximum monthly Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) payments cover most household sizes across the 48 contiguous states and Washington, D.C and the adjustment reflects changes in food costs and updates the income standards used to determine eligibility.

However, not everyone will receive the maximum benefit, as individual payments depend on household size, income and qualifying expenses. For households in the 48 contiguous states and Washington , D.C. , the new maximum monthly benefits for a one-person household is $306, an increase of $8 whilst a two-person household can receive up to $562, up $16. A three-person household can receive up to $808, an increase of $23 and a four-person household can receive a maximum of $1,023 per month, up $29. For a five-person household, the maximum is $1,217, an increase of $34. A six-person household can receive up to $1,463, up $42 and households with seven people can receive a maximum monthly benefit of $1,616, an increase of $45. For households of eight people, the maximum rises to $1,841, up $52. Alaska , Hawaii , Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands have separate allotments reflecting their different cost structures. For example, Hawaii 's maximum benefit for a four-person household decreased slightly to $1655. SNAP considers gross income before deductions and net income after allowable expenses, including certain housing, childcare and medical costs. Some states use broader eligibility rules, so applicants should check their state's requirements. Higher maximum allotments do not guarantee an increase of the same amount for every household, thus actual payments depend on individual circumstances, while the new income limits may affect whether households qualify for assistance.

How is SNAP funded in the United States?

SNAP is primarily federally funded through government revenue, with the U.S. Department of Agriculture overseeing the program and state agencies processing applications and distributing benefits through Electronic Benefit Transfer cards . The federal government pays the full cost of SNAP benefits, while states share administrative expenses and under legislation enacted in 2025, the federal contribution toward eligible state administrative costs fell from 50% to 25%, leaving states responsible for a larger share. Further changes are scheduled to introduce state contributions toward benefit costs from fiscal year 2028, linked to state payment error rates whilst for recipients.

articles.title: Donald Trump proposes changing the name of the Atlantic or the Pacific: What does he want to call it?
articles.standfirst: The President of the United States mentioned two names during a conference in Tennessee and once again put forward his idea of renaming oceans and gulfs.
articles.summary: The President of the United States mentioned two names during a conference in Tennessee and once again put forward his idea of renaming oceans and gulfs.
articles.body:
D onald Trump surprised attendees during a political event in Clarksville, Tennessee, by s uggesting that the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean could have another name. The president made the comment on Saturday, October 10, while reviewing the geographical changes promoted by his administration.

“We have the gulf, we have a beautiful lake, and now someone said we need a river” , he remarked to the audience. He then raised the possibility of adding an ocean to that list: “I was thinking about the Atlantic or the Pacific. We would call it ‘Trump Ocean’ or ‘Ocean of the Americas,’” he said. The proposal prompted laughter and applause from some of those in attendance.

“Trump Ocean” or “Ocean of the Americas”

The president joked about renaming the Atlantic or the Pacific, adding the proposal to the Gulf of America within his particular rhetorical style: He proposed “Trump Ocean,” which could be translated as «océano Trump», and “Ocean of the Americas” , that is, «océano de las Américas». He did not specify which of the two oceans he would choose, nor did he announce a formal measure to carry out the change.

The idea follows a similar line to other decisions by his administration. In January 2025, Trump ordered U.S. federal agencies to use the name “Gulf of America” instead of “Gulf of Mexico” . In August 2026, he also signed an order for Lake Ontario to be renamed “Lake America” in U.S. federal usage.

The president referred to that background to explain why he wanted to add an ocean and a river. However, he ruled out changing the name of the Hudson River and also assured that he would not change the Mississippi’s name. For now, he did not present a concrete proposal to rename either of the two oceans.

Can Trump officially change the name of an ocean?

The U.S. government can establish names for geographical features within its agencies and federal maps. However, a decision by Washington does not require other countries or international organizations to adopt the same name .

That was made clear by the previous changes: the name “Gulf of America” is used in certain official contexts in the United States, while other countries and media outlets retain “Gulf of Mexico.” In the case of Lake Ontario, the new U.S. designation also does not mean that Canada has to accept it.

For now, “Trump Ocean” and “Ocean of the Americas” are names mentioned during a speech, not official names for the Atlantic or the Pacific. The president did not announce an executive order or a formal procedure to change their names.

articles.title: New bombshell on Epstein's death: forensic expert debunks suicide story after reviewing autopsy files
articles.standfirst: Dr. Michael Freeman has questioned whether Jeffrey Epstein’s injuries can be explained by suicide
articles.summary: Dr. Michael Freeman has questioned whether Jeffrey Epstein’s injuries can be explained by suicide
articles.body:
A forensic medicine expert has raised fresh questions about Jeffrey Epstein ’s death after examining medical records that he says contain injuries inconsistent with the official explanation.

Dr. Michael Freeman , a fellow of the Royal College of Pathologists in London, told Metro that his independent review had identified details he believes could be consistent with a struggle or assault.

Freeman received the complete medical examiner’s file from Epstein’s brother, Mark, and has been preparing an independent report based on the material.

His findings are expected to be presented at a University College London law school event on November 16, after which he plans to release the complete file, including documents that have not previously been made public.

Speaking to Metro, Freeman questioned whether the evidence fully supported the conclusion reached by New York City’s medical examiner in 2019.

"There are lots of things that are not explained by a suicidal hanging, but are consistent with a potential struggle," Dr. Freeman said.

He also challenged the explanation for injuries documented in the medical records, saying: "He had injuries that could not possibly have been caused by a ligature," the doctor told the publication about what he learned from Epstein's body in the ME's report.

One of the most striking elements of Freeman’s assessment concerns marks reportedly visible above the ligature mark around Epstein’s neck.

The expert said that these appeared to resemble fingernail marks, potentially indicating that Epstein had tried to remove the material from his neck.

That interpretation, if supported by further examination, could become a central part of the debate surrounding the case. However, the reported findings have not overturned the official cause-of-death ruling, and Freeman’s conclusions remain an independent assessment that will need to be considered alongside the wider evidence.

The injuries that have renewed scrutiny of Epstein’s death

Freeman believes the autopsy records contain several unexplained features, including injuries to Epstein’s left shoulder, the area behind his neck and his face. He has also questioned the absence of photographs showing Epstein suspended in the position in which he was reportedly discovered.

The expert described the case as unusual, telling the publication that Epstein’s “death was completely unique in the annals of suicidal hanging descriptions”.

Freeman said his review focused on whether the injuries could reasonably have resulted from the circumstances in which Epstein was found. He said that some of the evidence was consistent with the possibility of a struggle, while acknowledging that other experts could disagree with his interpretation.

The medical examiner’s office has rejected any suggestion that the new claims have changed its position. In response to questions, the office said it stands by its determination that Epstein died by suicide.

Epstein was found dead in his cell at Manhattan’s Metropolitan Correctional Center on August 10, 2019.

He was awaiting trial on federal sex-trafficking charges, having been arrested the previous month. His death prevented the criminal case against him from proceeding to trial and intensified scrutiny of his connections to wealthy and influential individuals.

The official suicide ruling was issued by New York City Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Barbara Sampson on August 16, 2019. Debate about the autopsy findings has continued ever since, particularly over fractures involving structures in Epstein’s neck and whether those injuries can occur in different types of hanging or strangulation.

The significance of such injuries cannot be established in isolation. Medical examiners must assess the pattern of injuries, the ligature evidence, the circumstances of death and other available information before determining a cause.

The government’s earlier review concluded that the injuries were compatible with suicide, underscoring the disagreement between the existing official assessment and Freeman’s reported interpretation.

Mark Epstein backs an independent examination

Mark Epstein has welcomed the review, arguing that the medical evidence deserves detailed scientific scrutiny. He told CBS News that the team had spent months examining the records and comparing the findings with evidence from other deaths.

"They looked at this whole thing, they looked at it scientifically, they truly investigated this," he declared.

He also questioned whether the original ruling would have been reached had the material undergone the same level of examination earlier.

"The cause on Jeffrey's original death certificate – they further studied it in detail; this kind of study hasn't been done before," Mark explained. "If this kind of study had been done before, they wouldn't have come up with a suicide conclusion."

He added about Dr. Freeman 's findings, "This report was not done on my behalf; they did this of their own volition."

Freeman has also indicated that he wants the medical evidence to be available for public scrutiny, rather than asking audiences to accept his conclusions without seeing the material. The planned release could allow other forensic specialists to examine the records and assess whether the reported inconsistencies support his interpretation.

The new review comes against the backdrop of documented failures at the prison where Epstein died. A 2023 investigation by the Department of Justice’s Office of the Inspector General identified serious problems with staff supervision, required checks and security procedures.

Epstein had been left alone in his cell for hours before he was discovered. Nevertheless, the investigation concluded that he died by suicide and did not establish that another person killed him.

For now, Freeman’s findings represent a challenge to the official explanation, not proof that Epstein was murdered. The medical examiner’s office continues to stand by its original determination, and the full independent report has yet to be released.

The next stage will be whether Freeman’s complete analysis provides evidence that other specialists can independently verify. Until then, the competing interpretations of Epstein’s injuries must be distinguished from established findings about the circumstances of his death.
