articles.title: VA COLA Increase 2027: How Much Will Veterans' Disability Benefits Increase?
articles.standfirst: The COLA increase will officially be confirmed on Wednesday, October 14
articles.summary: The COLA increase will officially be confirmed on Wednesday, October 14
articles.body:
Veterans receiving disability compensation from the Department of Veterans Affairs could see higher monthly payments in 2027, with early estimates pointing to a Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) of around 3.5% to 3.8%.

The final increase will depend on the official calculation used for federal benefit adjustments and the adjustment is designed to help benefits keep pace with inflation, affecting veterans with service-connected disabilities and eligible dependents.

Estimates of the new COLA are generally around 3.4% to 3.8%, however, the projected figures remain estimates, and veterans should wait for the official announcement.

VA Disability Compensation is paid monthly and is tax-free. Eligibility depends on a service-connected condition and a VA Disability Rating , which runs from 0% to 100%. Payments may also vary based on eligible dependents.

Under the 3.8% projection for 2027, a veteran rated 10% would receive an estimated $187.28 per month, whilst a veteran rated 100% with no dependents would receive $4,088.25.

Veterans with ratings of 30% or higher may qualify for additional compensation based on a spouse, children, or dependent parents. The amount depends on family circumstances and the assigned rating, so estimates may not match an individual's payment.

September inflation data remain outstanding, meaning the official announcement will come on Wednesday, October 14 – thus, any rates are not an official rate approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs .

The projected rates are intended to take effect December 1 , with payments reflecting the increase generally arriving in January 2027 .

Will Social Security run out of money?

The future of Social Security in the United States remains a major financial and political concern, as the program faces growing pressure from an aging population, longer life expectancies and a changing balance between workers and retirees.

Social Security is primarily funded through payroll taxes paid by employees and employers. However, as millions of baby boomers retire and birth rates remain relatively low, fewer workers are supporting each beneficiary. This puts pressure on the program's trust funds, which help cover benefits when annual tax revenue falls short of total costs.

Social Security is not expected to simply disappear, even if its trust funds are depleted. Payroll taxes would continue flowing into the system, allowing the government to pay a substantial portion of scheduled benefits.

However, without legislative changes, beneficiaries could face automatic reductions once the relevant trust fund reserves are exhausted. For now, the Social Security Administration projects that the retirement and survivors' insurance trust fund will run out of reserves in late 2032.

At that point, ongoing income would cover approximately 78% of scheduled benefits unless lawmakers change the system. Congress could address the shortfall through measures such as increasing payroll taxes, adjusting the taxable earnings cap.

articles.title: California on alert for waves of up to 4.9 meters: “Never turn your back on the ocean”
articles.standfirst: The National Weather Service reported that dangerous conditions are expected on the beaches of the San Francisco Bay Area and also warns of possible coastal flooding through Tuesday.
articles.summary: The National Weather Service reported that dangerous conditions are expected on the beaches of the San Francisco Bay Area and also warns of possible coastal flooding through Tuesday.
articles.body:
Beaches in the San Francisco Bay Area remain under alert for hazardous conditions. The National Weather Service (NWS) warns of breaking waves of up to 16 feet, about 4.9 meters, in addition to strong rip currents and so-called sneaker waves, capable of catching even experienced people by surprise.

The warning will remain in effect until Monday night. The agency was unequivocal in its recommendation for those approaching the coast: “Never turn your back on the ocean” . It also urged people to stay out of the water and keep away from piers, jetties, rocks, and other structures along the shore.

Sneaker waves are waves that can be much larger than those that come before them and suddenly surge onto the beach. The danger is that they can appear after several minutes of seemingly calm surf and reach areas of sand that seemed safe.

The NWS warns that these waves can sweep people out to sea, including even experienced swimmers and surfers. The risk is now compounded by strong rip currents and especially high surf.

We want to reiterate how dangerous it is going to be along our Pacific coast this weekend

The warning affects sectors of the north coast of the Bay Area, Point Reyes National Seashore, and the coast of the San Francisco Peninsula. There are also advisories related to surf and flooding in San Francisco, Monterey Bay, and Big Sur.

Flood risk through Tuesday

"The surf is not the only threat. The NWS has a coastal flood advisory in effect until 3:00 p.m. Tuesday, October 13 for San Francisco, northern Monterey Bay, and southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur.

The agency anticipates up to 1.5 feet of flooding, about 46 centimeters, above ground level in low-lying areas near the coast and along waterways subject to the tides.

The combination of high tides and a higher-than-usual sea level can cause water to reach beaches, trails, roads, parking lots, and parks located along the coast. Authorities recommend not crossing flooded areas of unknown depth and to respect any closures or barricades.

California braces for a difficult winter

The current situation is also unfolding as scientists continue to closely monitor the conditions that could shape the winter in California. A strong El Niño event, combined with exceptionally high tides and rising sea levels, could trigger major episodes of erosion and flooding at different points along the coast.

One of the keys is a Kelvin wave associated with El Niño. This mass of warm water moves across the Pacific and can temporarily raise sea level off the western coast of the United States. According to experts cited by the Los Angeles Times, the effect could contribute to California recording some of the highest sea levels of its modern record this winter.

The problem arises when that higher baseline level coincides with high tides, large waves, and storms. Under those circumstances, the water can advance much farther over low-lying coastal areas and increase the erosion of beaches and cliffs.

For now, the NWS message is far more immediate: stay away from the water, avoid structures by the sea, and do not let your guard down during a seemingly calm swell period. Sneaker waves can arrive without warning.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday October 12 drawing for the $538 Million jackpot
articles.standfirst: One winner took home a big sum but did they claim the jackpot?
articles.summary: One winner took home a big sum but did they claim the jackpot?
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has climbed to $538 million after Saturday night's drawing produced no grand prize winner, setting up another opportunity for players on Monday. - however, anyone who wins faces substantial taxes. The winning numbers on Saturday were 1, 4, 19, 33, 51 and Powerball 15 . No ticket matched all six numbers, allowing the jackpot to grow ahead of the next drawing, scheduled for Monday at 22:59 ET/19:59 PT.

A Monday jackpot winner could choose between a $220.6 million lump-sum payment and the advertised $538 million prize distributed through 30 annual payments as the cash option provides immediate access to the money. However, it comes with a considerably smaller starting amount and federal taxes would reduce the lump sum sharply as the initial 24% withholding would leave approximately $167.6 million, before the winner's final federal income tax liability is calculated. At the highest federal tax rate, the after-tax amount could fall to around $139 million. Annuity offers a different payment structure, with 30 installments increasing by five percent annually. Federal taxes would still apply to the annuity too, reducing the total nominal payments to approximately $338.9 million under the estimates provided and state taxes could further reduce either option. That depends on where the winning ticket was purchased and the winner's tax circumstances. For example, New York has a high state income tax rate of 10.9%, whilst states including Texas , California , Florida and Alaska do not levy state income tax on lottery winnings in the same way.

Can players improve their chances of winning Powerball?

The jackpot's size does not change the mathematical challenge facing players. Each standard $2 ticket has jackpot odds of approximately 1 in 292.2 million, requiring five correct white-ball numbers from 69 possibilities and the correct red Powerball from 26. Players can increase their chances by purchasing additional tickets with distinct combinations, although the improvement remains small relative to the enormous odds. For example, buying 100 different combinations for one drawing would still leave the jackpot probability at roughly 1 in 2.92 million. Lottery pools allow participants to purchase more combinations collectively, but any prize must be shared among the group. Selecting less popular numbers might reduce the likelihood of splitting a jackpot with other winners, but it cannot make a combination more likely to be drawn. The overall odds of winning any Powerball prize are approximately 1 in 24.9. Saturday's drawing included a $1 million winner in California , demonstrating that prizes below the jackpot remain possible, although substantial wins are far from guaranteed. Powerball 's largest jackpot of 2026 so far reached $1.04 billion, claimed by a player in Illinois in August. Monday's drawing offers another chance at a life-changing sum, but the sensible approach remains treating tickets as entertainment rather than a financial plan.

articles.title: Man dies at Six Flags Over Georgia as police investigate accident
articles.standfirst: Georgia 2026.
articles.summary: What happened?
articles.body:
On Monday, October 12, as many people enjoyed the Columbus Day holiday, an emergency disrupted the day at Six Flags Over Georgia .

A man died after falling from Goliath , one of the park’s main roller coasters. Authorities also reported several people injured, although they have not provided details about how those injuries occurred.

Some visitors told CNN affiliate WXIA that they witnessed the fall. Aerial footage released by the station showed other riders being evacuated from the roller coaster after the incident.

Six Flags expresses its condolences

Following the incident, Six Flags Over Georgia expressed its sorrow and extended its condolences to the visitor’s family and loved ones .

“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today”

"Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected."

When will the park reopen?

Six Flags Over Georgia will remain closed until further notice. According to its regular October schedule, the park does not open on weekdays, making Monday, October 12, an exception because of the Columbus Day holiday.

articles.title: How much are VA Education benefits increasing with the 2027 COLA? What to know about with the latest projection
articles.standfirst: The Cost-of-Living-Adjustment will be confirmed on October 14
articles.summary: The Cost-of-Living-Adjustment will be confirmed on October 14
articles.body:
Veterans and eligible military family members are receiving higher monthly education benefits following payment increases that took effect October 1 as the adjustments raise support available through two Department of Veterans Affairs programs. Helping recipients cover education-related costs, students enrolled in the Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty program can now receive up to $2,601 monthly, an increase of $83 – and full-time participants in Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA) qualify for payments of up to $1,621, representing a $47 increase.

The Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty benefit is for qualifying veterans who served at least two years of active-duty service in total and the amount paid can also vary with the length of that service. Whilst the DEA is available to eligible spouses and children of veterans or service members who have died, are captured or missing, or have a permanent and total service-connected disability. The program helps qualifying family members pursue education. Monthly payments vary with enrollment and service history. GI Bill rates differ depending on whether a veteran completed two years or three or more years on active duty, while the number of classes taken also affects the amount a student receives. These rates are in effect from October 1, but they should not be mistaken for a confirmed forecast of the Cost-of-Living-Adjustment increase in 2027, which is not due until Wednesday, October 14. Estimates have the COLA rising between 3.4% and 3.8%.

What students should know about the new rates

The DEA increase adds $564 over 12 months of full-time enrolment and that extra support can help eligible military dependents manage education and daily living costs as the money can go toward housing, meal plans, transportation, books and other education-related expenses. However, the maximum monthly rate is not guaranteed for every student, because individual benefits depend on eligibility and enrollment. GI Bill recipients should also consider the program's time limit. The benefit must be used within 10 years after discharge, making it important for veterans to check their remaining eligibility before planning education costs. As a means of preparation, students should compare the maximum with their own award and course load before assuming how much will arrive each month. The new rates raise the available support, but the individual payment depends on program rules and personal circumstances but overall, the latest rates provide up to $83 more per month for Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty students and up to $47 more for full-time DEA participants.

articles.title: New twist in the Lindsay Clancy case: The hospital refuses to take responsibility for her treatment
articles.standfirst: The Women & Infants Hospital of Rhode Island rejects Clancy’s malpractice lawsuit
articles.summary: The Women & Infants Hospital of Rhode Island rejects Clancy’s malpractice lawsuit
articles.body:
The Women & Infants Hospital of Rhode Island is pushing back against Lindsay Clancy ’s medical malpractice lawsuit, raising 26 affirmative defenses in a new court filing as the hospital disputes responsibility for the damages she alleges, setting up another battle over her psychiatric treatment.

The October 2 response addresses Clancy ’s second amended complaint, invoking comparative negligence, informed consent, third-party responsibility and intervening causes.

The filing outlines the hospital’s legal defenses but does not establish that Clancy was negligent or that her conduct caused her children’s deaths and among its arguments, the hospital asserts that she was informed about treatment risks, possible consequences and available alternatives.

Its response comes as she pursues claims against medical professionals over the psychiatric care she received before the January 2023 tragedy but Clancy ’s civil attorney, Andrew Meyer Jr. cautioned against reading the filing as a meaningful determination of the case’s merits.

"It's more form than it is substance, and it's of course our burden to prove the case," Meyer told RadarOnline.com. "The defense begins their case by denying everything and saying prove it. This is just the first step, and it's just classic, and I wouldn't read anything into it.”

Meyer said the parties have yet to establish whether the alleged treatment failures occurred, emphasizing that evidence will be examined as the litigation progresses.

The tragedy of the Clancy children and questions over psychiatric care

articles.title: 2027 tax refund: How families with two children could qualify for up to $7,316
articles.standfirst: The maximum Earned Income Tax Credit applies to eligible 2026 earnings and must be claimed on a 2027 tax return
articles.summary: The maximum Earned Income Tax Credit applies to eligible 2026 earnings and must be claimed on a 2027 tax return
articles.body:
Some families with two qualifying children may be eligible for up to $7,316 through the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) . The amount is for income earned in 2026 and claimed on a federal tax return filed in 2027. It is a maximum, not a guaranteed payment: the credit depends on income, filing status and eligibility.

To qualify, a taxpayer must have earned income, such as wages, tips or self-employment income, and meet the IRS’s income limits. For two qualifying children, the credit reaches zero at $65,899 for married couples filing jointly and $58,629 for most other filing statuses. Investment income must not exceed $12,200 for 2026.

Who can claim the credit?

A child must meet the IRS rules for relationship, age and residency, including generally living with the taxpayer in the United States for more than half the year. Taxpayers claiming the credit with a child also need valid Social Security numbers for themselves and the child.

The $7,316 maximum is available at certain income levels. For a family with two qualifying children, it is reached when earned income reaches $18,290. The credit then begins to phase out as income rises. Families can claim the EITC on Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR; those claiming a qualifying child must also file Schedule EIC.

The EITC is refundable, which means eligible taxpayers may receive money even if the credit is larger than the income tax they owe. The credit first offsets any tax owed, and any remaining amount can be included in the tax refund. It is not a separate payment that the IRS automatically sends to every family.

When could the money arrive?

Taxpayers will claim the credit when filing their 2026 tax return in 2027. By law, the IRS cannot issue refunds that include the EITC before mid-February.

Direct deposit is available, and the IRS is phasing out paper refund checks, but processing times vary. Taxpayers can check their refund status through the IRS’s Where’s My Refund? tool.

articles.title: COLA Increase 2027: What is the adjustment for next year and how much extra payment you'll get in your Social Security?
articles.standfirst: Social Security recipients could see their monthly payments rise by around 3.5% in 2027
articles.summary: Social Security recipients could see their monthly payments rise by around 3.5% in 2027
articles.body:
Millions of Americans receiving Social Security are waiting to find out how much more money they could receive next year, with the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) expected to deliver a larger increase than the one implemented in January 2026.

The Senior Citizens League (TSCL) , a nonpartisan seniors' advocacy organization, currently projects a 3.5% increase for 2027. If that forecast proves accurate, it would represent a 0.7-percentage-point rise compared with the 2.8% adjustment beneficiaries received in 2026.

However, the figure remains a projection until the Social Security Administration (SSA) confirms the official adjustment. The announcement is expected on Wednesday, October 14, following the release of September inflation figures by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Those figures complete the data needed to calculate the annual increase.

For retirees already dealing with higher grocery bills, housing costs, utility expenses and medical spending, the announcement could have a meaningful impact on household budgets.

Nevertheless, the size of the increase will depend on the final inflation calculation, and a higher monthly payment does not necessarily mean recipients will feel substantially better off financially.

The previous adjustment took effect at the beginning of 2026, raising Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits by 2.8%.

A 3.5% increase would therefore provide a more substantial boost next year, although it would remain well below the exceptional 8.7% adjustment introduced in 2023.

How much more money could beneficiaries receive in 2027?

The amount added to each person's monthly payment will depend on the benefit they currently receive. Under the 3.5% projection, the increase would be calculated by multiplying the existing monthly benefit by 0.035.

According to TSCL's September estimate, the average monthly Social Security benefit was $1,940.08. If the forecast becomes official, that payment would increase by approximately $67.90, bringing the monthly total to around $2,007.98.

Here are some examples of what the projected adjustment could mean for different monthly payments:

$1,000 benefit: an extra $35 per month, bringing the payment to $1,035.

$1,500 benefit: an extra $52.50 per month, bringing the payment to $1,552.50.

$1,940 benefit: an extra $67.90 per month, bringing the payment to approximately $2,007.90.

$2,000 benefit: an extra $70 per month, bringing the payment to $2,070.

$2,500 benefit: an extra $87.50 per month, bringing the payment to $2,587.50.

These examples are estimates based on a 3.5% adjustment, rather than confirmation of individual payments. The final increase may differ if the official COLA is higher or lower.

The adjustment is designed to help Social Security benefits keep pace with inflation. The SSA bases its calculation on changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, known as CPI-W.

Specifically, it compares the average index for July, August and September with the corresponding average from the third quarter of the previous year used in the calculation.

This formula means the final September inflation reading is particularly important. Forecasts from advocacy groups and financial publications provide an indication of the likely outcome, but they cannot replace the government's official figure.

The 2027 adjustment will also affect eligible people receiving SSI, a separate program that provides payments to people with limited income and resources who are aged, blind or disabled. The COLA applies to more than retirement benefits alone, although individual payment amounts and eligibility circumstances vary.

Why the increase might not feel as large as expected

Even if the 3.5% projection is confirmed, some beneficiaries may find that the additional money does not fully cover their rising expenses.

Housing, food, transportation and healthcare can absorb much of a monthly increase, particularly for older Americans who rely heavily on Social Security as their main source of income.

There is also the question of Medicare premiums. For beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare Part B, any increase in the standard premium could reduce the amount of the COLA that remains in their pocket. The precise effect will depend on the applicable premium and the individual's circumstances.

The calculation itself has also attracted criticism. TSCL argues that CPI-W does not necessarily reflect the spending patterns of older Americans, whose budgets may devote a greater share to healthcare and other essential costs. The organization has highlighted the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly, or CPI-E, as a possible alternative measure.

For now, the key number to watch is the official 2027 COLA announcement. If the anticipated 3.5% increase is confirmed, it would offer millions of recipients a larger monthly payment than they received in 2026.

The final figure, however, will determine exactly how much additional support beneficiaries can expect when the adjustment takes effect in January 2027.

articles.title: John D. Rockefeller, American businessman and philanthropist: "Don't be afraid to give up the good to go for the great"
articles.standfirst: The famous motivational saying encourages people to move beyond familiar success in pursuit of greater ambitions
articles.summary: The famous motivational saying encourages people to move beyond familiar success in pursuit of greater ambitions
articles.body:
“Don't be afraid to give up the good to go for the great” is a popular expression about ambition, personal development and the difficult decisions that can separate ordinary achievements from extraordinary ones.

The message is straightforward: reaching a satisfactory level of success should not necessarily mark the end of a person's ambitions.

Sometimes, making meaningful progress requires leaving behind a situation that is comfortable, rewarding or familiar to pursue an opportunity with greater potential.

The saying is commonly associated with John D. Rockefeller , the American businessman who built Standard Oil into one of the most powerful companies in the United States and later became one of the country's most influential philanthropists.

It appears under his name on quotation websites, including Goodreads, and has circulated widely in discussions about business and personal achievement.

However, there is an important distinction between a quote's popularity and the evidence supporting its authorship. The saying's connection to Rockefeller has not been firmly established, and quotation researchers have questioned whether he actually said it.

That uncertainty does not diminish the idea's appeal. Its central lesson remains relevant to people considering a career change, entrepreneurs looking to expand their businesses or anyone who believes their current circumstances no longer reflect their full potential.

The thinking behind the quote and Rockefeller's remarkable career

Rockefeller's life offers a compelling backdrop for a saying about ambition, although there is no verified evidence that he personally expressed this particular sentiment.

Born in New York in 1839, Rockefeller began his professional life in bookkeeping before entering the oil-refining industry during the 1860s. In 1870, he helped establish Standard Oil, a company that would grow to dominate much of the American petroleum business.

His approach centred on efficiency, organisation and controlling different stages of the oil industry.

Standard Oil expanded rapidly, acquiring competitors and developing an extensive network of refineries, transportation arrangements and distribution operations. By the late nineteenth century, it had become an industrial powerhouse.

Rockefeller's business methods were also controversial. Critics challenged the company's concentration of economic power and its treatment of competitors.

In 1911, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Standard Oil violated federal antitrust law, resulting in the breakup of its parent corporation.

His legacy, therefore, is more complicated than a simple story of success. He was an exceptionally effective business builder, but his rise also became a defining example in the debate over monopolies, competition and corporate power.

The quote's message is particularly interesting when considered in that context. The idea of abandoning what is already working in favour of something better can apply to business strategy, but it should not be confused with taking risks indiscriminately.

Successful decisions often require research, patience and an understanding of what could be lost as well as gained.

For an entrepreneur, this might mean replacing an outdated business model with a more sustainable one.

For an employee, it could involve pursuing a new position that offers greater responsibility or opportunities to learn. In personal life, it might mean recognising that a comfortable routine no longer supports long-term goals.

Why the quote continues to resonate

One reason the saying has endured is that it challenges the tendency to become satisfied with achievements once they arrive. Reaching a goal can bring stability and confidence, but it can also make change feel unnecessarily risky.

The phrase encourages people to assess whether their current situation is genuinely the best option available or simply the easiest one to maintain. That distinction matters because progress sometimes requires giving up short-term comfort for a potentially greater long-term reward.

Still, the message should not be interpreted as an instruction to abandon every successful arrangement in search of something bigger.

A good opportunity can be worth protecting, and not every new possibility will produce a better outcome. The most useful interpretation is to remain open to improvement while weighing the risks carefully.

There is also a question of attribution. Wikiquote lists “Don't be afraid to give up the good to go for the great” among disputed Rockefeller quotations. Its research notes that an early published appearance identified the country singer Kenny Rogers, while the connection to Rockefeller emerged later. The saying's precise original author remains uncertain.

That makes it more accurate to describe the line as widely attributed to Rockefeller rather than a verified quotation from him.

Rockefeller himself left a substantial written record, including his 1909 memoir, Random Reminiscences of Men and Events.

Yet the famous wording has not been established as part of that work. This is a useful reminder that familiar quotations can become attached to celebrated figures over time, even when the original source is missing.

Ultimately, the enduring value of the saying lies in the question it asks of its audience: is a satisfactory result enough, or is there a realistic opportunity to achieve something better?

Whether the words originated with Rockefeller , Kenny Rogers or another unidentified author, they capture a challenge faced by people in almost every field.

Growth requires recognising when an existing achievement has served its purpose and deciding, with care and conviction, whether the next opportunity is worth pursuing.

articles.title: When will the 2027 COLA increase take effect? Here's when you'll get more money
articles.standfirst: Social Security beneficiaries should see their cost-of-living adjustment reflected in payments beginning in January 2027
articles.summary: Social Security beneficiaries should see their cost-of-living adjustment reflected in payments beginning in January 2027
articles.body:
Millions of Americans receiving Social Security are preparing for the next annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) , which is designed to help benefits keep pace with inflation.

While the Social Security Administration is expected to announce the 2027 adjustment on October 14, 2026, recipients will have to wait until the new year to see the increase reflected in their regular retirement payments.

The timing is important for retirees, people receiving disability benefits and others who rely on Social Security to cover everyday expenses.

The annual adjustment changes monthly benefit amounts rather than delivering a separate one-time bonus, meaning eligible recipients generally receive a higher payment each month once the new rates take effect.

The Senior Citizens League has projected a 3.5% COLA for 2027. If that estimate is confirmed, it would exceed the 2.8% adjustment that took effect in January 2026.

However, the projection is not the final decision: the official increase depends on inflation data used by the government to calculate the adjustment.

For most people receiving retirement benefits, January 2027 will be the first month covered by the higher payment rate.

The exact date the money arrives in a bank account depends on the Social Security payment schedule, which generally varies according to a recipient's birth date and, in some cases, when they first began receiving benefits.

It is therefore important to distinguish between the month the higher benefit applies to and the date the money reaches an individual's account. Although the increase takes effect for January benefits, not every beneficiary will receive their payment on January 1.

When will the higher Social Security payment arrive?

The first increased payments are scheduled for January 2027. Social Security retirement benefits are typically paid on Wednesdays, with the specific Wednesday determined by the beneficiary's birth date.

Under the usual schedule, people born from the 1st through the 10th of a month generally receive their payments on the second Wednesday.

Those born from the 11th through the 20th are usually paid on the third Wednesday, while beneficiaries born from the 21st through the 31st generally receive their money on the fourth Wednesday.

That means many retirement beneficiaries should expect their first payment reflecting the 2027 COLA on a Wednesday in January. The precise date will depend on their payment group and the official calendar.

There are exceptions. People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997, as well as certain recipients who receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) , may follow a different payment schedule.

SSI payments are normally issued at the beginning of the month, and the January 2027 payment calendar may differ if a scheduled date falls on a weekend or federal holiday. Beneficiaries should check their individual schedules rather than assume everyone will receive the increase on the same day.

The adjustment is calculated using inflation data from the third quarter of the year.

The government compares the average Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) for July, August and September with the corresponding period used for the previous calculation. The resulting percentage determines how much monthly Social Security benefits rise.

The September inflation report is therefore a key part of the process. Forecasts can give beneficiaries an idea of what to expect, but the official adjustment cannot be established until the relevant data are available and the Social Security Administration announces its decision.

articles.standfirst: Powerball players are waiting for Wednesday night's drawing, with the estimated jackpot reaching $562 million and a cash option of $230.4 million
articles.summary: Powerball players are waiting for Wednesday night's drawing, with the estimated jackpot reaching $562 million and a cash option of $230.4 million
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $562 million ahead of Wednesday, October 14's drawing, giving ticket holders across the United States another opportunity to win one of the country's biggest lottery prizes.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, with players hoping to match all five white balls and the red Powerball to claim the grand prize.

articles.title: Who is Hassan Kariem? The man who died after falling from the Goliath roller coaster in front of his son
articles.standfirst: The 42-year-old Atlanta-area educator was remembered by his sister as “my hero” after the fatal incident at Six Flags Over Georgia
articles.summary: The 42-year-old Atlanta-area educator was remembered by his sister as “my hero” after the fatal incident at Six Flags Over Georgia
articles.body:
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem , the man who died after falling from the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia , was an educator and devoted family member whose life had already included several serious challenges.

The 42-year-old's death on Monday, October 12, shocked visitors at the amusement park near Atlanta and prompted an investigation by local and state authorities.

As his relatives began to grieve, his sister Andrea Clark spoke about the man she knew, describing him as a source of inspiration and someone whose presence had shaped her life.

“He’s an amazing person,” Clark said through tears, as per the New York Post. “The coolest part about me was him,” she added, recalling the closeness of their relationship.

Clark , 35, described her brother as “my hero” and struggled to understand how he could have died after overcoming major health challenges in earlier years.

Kariem had battled cancer, which went into remission in 2015, according to his sister. She also revealed that he had survived a serious car fire approximately a month before the roller coaster incident.

“He had other issues, but he’s healthy, he was able-bodied. I don’t understand it,” Clark said.

For his family, the loss was particularly difficult given the obstacles Kariem had already overcome. His sister's account portrayed a man who continued to work hard, care for those close to him and build a life after confronting serious adversity.

“He could do it all,” she said as she wept.

What happened to Hassan Kariem on Goliath roller coaster?

The fatal incident occurred at approximately 3:58 p.m. on October 12 at Six Flags Over Georgia in Cobb County, Georgia. Police officers responding to the scene found Kariem beneath the ride, unresponsive and not breathing.

According to witnesses and park employees, Kariem was ejected from the roller coaster and struck other visitors before falling beneath the attraction. Several other people were reported injured.

Authorities haven't yet established the precise circumstances that led to his fall. Investigators from the Cobb County Police Department's Major Crimes Unit are examining the incident, while state safety officials are also investigating.

The ride involved was Goliath , a major attraction that rises approximately 200 feet and reaches speeds of around 70 mph.

The scale and speed of the hypercoaster have placed particular attention on the questions surrounding how Kariem came out of his seat and whether the restraint system, operating procedures or another factor contributed to the tragedy. No definitive cause has been announced.

Six Flags confirmed that it was cooperating with authorities and expressed condolences to Kariem 's family, friends and loved ones. The park also said it was supporting visitors and employees affected by the incident.

The company subsequently closed nine similar roller coasters across six parks in the United States and Canada as a precaution. The decision was described as being made “out of an abundance of caution” while the investigation continued.

The closures were a safety measure and did not, by themselves, establish that a defect had caused the fatal incident.

Kariem 's family has also faced the distress of images and videos circulating online. Clark appealed to people sharing graphic footage of her brother's final moments to stop.

“That’s just evil,” she said. “It’s tragic and I feel like we’ve gone too far as a society.”

Her plea highlighted another painful aspect of the tragedy: relatives must cope with their loss while confronting disturbing material being shared publicly.

Teacher remembered for commitment to family

Away from the amusement park, Kariem was known for his work in education and technology. Reports identified him as an Atlanta-area educator who worked at Wesley International Academy , where he was associated with technology instruction and supporting students.

His professional life was one part of a broader commitment to helping others. His sister said he worked hard and took care of his family, including his fiancée's daughter, who had been in his life since she was three years old.

Clark explained that although her brother didn't have a son of his own, he had played an important role in raising and supporting the child in his family.

Some reports have described a child being present during the roller coaster incident, although accounts of the family relationships have not been entirely consistent. The details of the incident remain under investigation.

The family's memories of Kariem have increasingly centered on the person he was outside his final moments: a brother, partner, educator and trusted presence in the lives of people close to him.

His death has also renewed questions about amusement park safety and the protections intended to keep riders secure. Investigators will need to establish what happened before any conclusions can be drawn about responsibility or the cause of the fall.

For Clark and the rest of Kariem 's loved ones, however, the immediate reality is the loss of someone they considered irreplaceable. Her recollections of his resilience, generosity and dedication to family have offered a personal picture of the man behind the headlines.

As authorities continue their work, Kariem 's family is left to mourn a life that his sister says had already overcome extraordinary difficulties. Her tribute is a reminder that beyond the investigation and the questions surrounding Goliath , a family has lost someone it deeply loved.

articles.title: Criticism and mockery directed at Katie Zacharia, Donald Trump's new press secretary: She's being compared to AI avatar
articles.standfirst: The new White House spokesperson answered just three questions during a 14-minute appearance
articles.summary: The new White House spokesperson answered just three questions during a 14-minute appearance
articles.body:
Katie Zacharia had barely finished her first White House press briefing before critics began questioning whether President Donald Trump 's newly appointed spokesperson was ready for one of Washington's most demanding jobs.

The 41-year-old spent approximately 14 minutes at the podium Tuesday, delivering prepared remarks about the administration's achievements before answering three questions and bringing the session to an abrupt conclusion.

Her delivery attracted immediate criticism, with commentators highlighting her reliance on written notes, limited eye contact and occasional awkward pauses during the appearance.

Guardian correspondent David Smith compared her presentation to an AI avatar, a description that quickly became part of the online discussion surrounding her debut.

First briefing takes unexpected turn

Zacharia opened by expressing her enthusiasm for joining the administration, telling reporters she had wanted to work for President Trump for a considerable time.

"I am so honored to work for President Trump and the American people," she said before discussing Republican campaigning ahead of the November midterm elections.

She praised turnout at the president's rallies, claiming that supporters were attending events in record numbers, although those assertions faced scrutiny from political commentators.

The questioning then shifted toward foreign policy, with Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy asking whether the United States had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

"I will have to get back to you on that," Zacharia replied, declining to provide an immediate clarification about the administration's position.

Her most substantial announcement concerned US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle , whose departure had become the subject of speculation.

"We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign. She has been a wonderful asset to the team and we wish her well," Zacharia confirmed.

Answer sparks online mockery

Another uncomfortable moment came when a reporter asked how Zacharia planned to balance her new responsibilities with raising four children.

While discussing her husband's support, she accidentally referred to him as the president before correcting herself.

"So my president, excuse me, my husband, that's a good one," Zacharia said, acknowledging the verbal mistake.

She subsequently praised Trump for appointing women with families to senior administration positions, arguing that his decision demonstrated confidence in their ability to manage demanding careers.

The briefing ended shortly afterward, prompting further criticism from commentators who questioned why the new press secretary had answered so few questions.

President Trump praises Zacharia despite criticism

Political opponents quickly seized on the appearance, with the anti-Trump Lincoln Project sharing a comparison to former British prime minister Liz Truss.

Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci also joined the discussion, referring to his own brief tenure during Trump's first administration.

"The clock is running. Thus far 1/11th of a Scaramucci," he wrote on X, referencing his departure after just 11 days in the position.

Trump , however, rejected the negative assessments surrounding Zacharia 's introduction, offering a straightforward endorsement of his latest appointment.

"I thought she was very good," the president said.

Zacharia previously worked in communications for Trump Media and Technology Group and briefly served at the Department of Homeland Security before receiving the White House appointment.

Her debut has generated considerable attention, but the longer-term assessment of her performance will depend on how she handles future briefings and questions from reporters.

articles.title: Video captures the moment Tupac Shakur's killer receives his sentence of 40 years to life
articles.standfirst: Thirty years later, Duane "Keffe D" Davis was found guilty and sentenced for Tupac's death
articles.summary: Thirty years later, Duane "Keffe D" Davis was found guilty and sentenced for Tupac's death
articles.body:
On September 7, 1996, the hip-hop world was forever reshaped when legendary artist Tupac Shakur was gunned down in a drive-by shooting off the Las Vegas Strip at just 25 years old .

Cut down at the absolute peak of his global stardom, shortly after releasing his seminal multi-platinum album All Eyez on Me and starring in major feature films, Shakur succumbed to his injuries six days later.

For nearly three decades, his tragic death remained one of pop culture’s most enduring unsolved cold cases , spawning endless conspiracy theories and intense public intrigue. However, law enforcement finally closed the loop on the historic mystery, culminating in the trial and conviction of the sole mastermind responsible for orchestrating the fatal attack.

Video Captures Courtroom Milestone: "Keffe D." Davis Sentenced to 40 Years

Courtroom video footage captured the momentous conclusion of the nearly 30-year investigation as former gang leader Duane "Keffe D" Davis stood before Clark County District Court Judge Carli Kierny to receive a sentence of 40 years to life in prison .

The 63-year-old was convicted of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon for organizing the retaliatory drive-by shooting following a casino brawl involving his late nephew, Orlando Anderson .

Although Davis was not accused of pulling the trigger himself, prosecutors proved he provided the firearm and directed the occupants of the white Cadillac that pulled alongside Shakur's vehicle.

His self-incriminating statements in interviews and his published memoir ultimately sealed his fate, with Judge Kierny granting him credit for time served while admonishing him prior to handing down the maximum sentence.

The emotional sentencing featured powerful victim impact statements from Shakur's family members, including his sister, Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur , who expressed that the devastating loss had crippled their family for decades and stolen a visionary who fought for his community.

When offered an opportunity to make a final statement to the court, Davis coldly declined, stating, "I'm good. I'm gonna appeal this case for sure" . While his defense team prepares an appeal, the historic ruling provides long-awaited accountability for hip-hop fans worldwide, cementing a definitive legal resolution for one of music history's most tragic losses.

articles.title: Melinda French Gates and her daughters join a $100 million mission to help women get the care they need
articles.standfirst: Jennifer and Phoebe are backing a global fund supporting 22 organizations working on maternal health, reproductive care and protection from violence
articles.summary: Jennifer and Phoebe are backing a global fund supporting 22 organizations working on maternal health, reproductive care and protection from violence
articles.body:
M elinda French Gates has spent years pushing for better health care and greater opportunity for women. Now, her daughters Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates are joining her in that work as founding supporters of the Women’s Health Co-Lab, a collaborative fund aiming to raise $100 million for women and girls around the world. The three are part of a larger group that includes 14 other donors.

The fund launched with more than $70 million committed, according to ICONIQ Impact, which created the initiative with Co-Impact. Its 22 grantee organizations will receive flexible, multiyear funding over three years. That means the groups can direct the money toward their most pressing needs as they work to improve care and the systems around it.

A family commitment with a global reach

The organizations focus on three connected areas: maternal health, sexual and reproductive health, and gender-based violence. Their work includes strengthening pregnancy and childbirth care, expanding access to family planning and reproductive health information, and supporting survivors of violence. Among the grantees are Every Mother Counts, Girl Effect, GIRE in Mexico, Serenas and Ujamaa Africa.

The mission is personal for all three women. Jennifer is a pediatric resident, and she and her mother used the final days of Jennifer’s maternity leave to visit Louisiana and hear from patients, health care providers, lawmakers and mothers who had lost babies. Phoebe, co-founder of fashion platform Phia, has also spoken publicly about reproductive rights and traveled to Louisiana and Mississippi to learn how abortion restrictions affect women.

Phoebe said the 22 organizations offer “reason to believe change is possible,” pointing to their work to protect reproductive freedom, confront violence and improve care for mothers. The fund’s structure also reflects the organizers’ emphasis on trusting local leaders to shape solutions in their own communities.

The Co-Lab is one part of Melinda French Gates’ wider commitment to women’s health. In June 2026, she announced a separate $215 million in funding through Pivotal, bringing her total support for women’s health to more than $600 million over two years. That commitment is separate from the Co-Lab’s $100 million goal.

For the Gates women, the fund brings a shared family concern into a much larger effort . Its success will depend on reaching the full $100 million goal and on whether the organizations receiving support can turn that money into better care, greater safety and more choices for women and girls.

articles.title: Costco Food Court Menu for Fall: every new item you can get during this season
articles.standfirst: Costco is bringing autumn flavours to its food court with a new Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae, while the much-loved churro is also back for a limited time
articles.summary: Costco is bringing autumn flavours to its food court with a new Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae, while the much-loved churro is also back for a limited time
articles.body:
C ostco shoppers looking for a seasonal treat have a new reason to visit the food court this fall. The warehouse retailer has introduced a Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae , combining classic autumn flavours with its familiar vanilla soft-serve ice cream.

The new dessert is priced at $2.99 and has started appearing at food courts across the United States. It arrives as Costco refreshes its rotating selection of specialty sundaes, replacing the summer's Strawberry Shortcake Sundae with a dessert inspired by one of fall's most recognisable flavours.

Availability may vary between warehouses, and the retailer has not announced a definitive end date for the limited-time offering.

The launch is particularly appealing to shoppers who enjoy apple pie served with ice cream. Rather than ordering a traditional slice of pie alongside a separate dessert, customers can get the combination in a single cup while making their usual Costco shopping trip.

Another familiar food court favourite has also returned: the churro. Together, the two additions give customers a couple of sweet options to look out for as temperatures fall and seasonal menus begin to change.

Every new Costco food court item to try this fall

1. Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae — $2.99

The headline addition is the Vanilla Apple Pie Sundae , a dessert built around three main components: vanilla soft serve, apple pie filling and pieces of pie crust.

The ice cream provides a creamy base, while the apple topping brings the sweet, fruity flavour associated with homemade apple pie. Pie crust pieces add a contrasting texture, giving the dessert a little crunch alongside the soft ice cream and filling.

The combination takes inspiration from apple pie à la mode, the classic pairing of pie and ice cream. Costco's version is served in a cup, making it a convenient option for customers who want something sweet after a hot dog, pizza slice or other food court meal.

Early reactions from shoppers and food reviewers have been enthusiastic, particularly about the amount of apple topping in each serving. Some have compared it favourably with other seasonal sundaes, although taste preferences will naturally differ.

The $2.99 price keeps it within the food court's relatively inexpensive dessert range. However, anyone planning a visit specifically to try the sundae should check their local warehouse, since reports indicate that availability is still rolling out and may not be uniform.

Costco has also brought back its churro after removing the snack from its regular food court menu in 2024.

The return was announced by chief financial officer Gary Millerchip during the company's September earnings call, with the treat set to return to US locations for a limited period beginning in October.

The long, twisted pastry is coated in cinnamon sugar and offers a familiar alternative to the new apple dessert. Its return has attracted attention from customers who missed it after the food court replaced it with a warm chocolate chunk cookie.

The churro's texture has divided some fans, with reviews varying between those who enjoy its softer, doughier consistency and those who prefer a crunchier pastry. Nevertheless, its comeback gives shoppers another seasonal sweet option alongside the sundae.

The new seasonal treats join a menu that still includes established favourites such as the $1.50 hot dog and soda combination, pizza and other familiar food court options.

These core items remain distinct from the specialty desserts, which Costco periodically changes to introduce new flavours and encourage repeat visits.

The seasonal sundae rotation has previously included options such as Strawberry Shortcake, Double Chocolate Mint, Caramel Churro and Vanilla Cookie Crunch. The same advice applies to the returning churro. Seasonal availability can vary, and individual warehouse menus may differ.

For now, the apple pie sundae is the standout new addition, offering an easy way to enjoy familiar autumn flavours without buying a whole pie. The churro's return adds a nostalgic alternative for customers who prefer cinnamon sugar to fruit toppings.

Anyone hoping to try both should check the menu at their local Costco before making a special trip. With the sundae priced at $2.99 and the churro around $1.50, the two treats offer affordable ways to sample the food court's latest seasonal changes.

articles.title: Donald Trump considers using the MOAB, the mother of all bombs, against Iran: 10,000 kilograms and the explosive power of eleven tons of TNT
articles.standfirst: The United States is considering launching a forceful attack on its energy infrastructure
articles.summary: The United States is considering launching a forceful attack on its energy infrastructure
articles.body:
The conflict between the United States and Iran continues unabated. The U.S. military does not rule out, according to sources consulted by CNN , using the so-called MOAB to attack its energy and nuclear infrastructure. The acronym MOAB stands for Massive Ordnance Air Blast and it is popularly known as the mother of all bombs .

These attack plans, if carried out, would represent a turning point in the conflict between the United States and Iran , according to CNN's analysis. The aforementioned outlet maintains that Donald Trump is being pressured to bring the conflict to an end, and his advisers describe the use of the MOAB as a "decisive" step. Everything indicates, in any case, that the White House will not make any abrupt changes in direction until the midterm elections are held, next November 3 .

Trump would send a symbolic message by using the MOAB

CNN, after speaking with several officials familiar with the situation, notes that some of them do not consider using the MOAB to be truly effective in destroying Iran's nuclear infrastructure. Despite its great destructive power, it would not have, according to these sources, sufficient penetration capability to destroy certain facilities.

Beyond its effectiveness from a military standpoint, the aforementioned outlet suggests that the use of these weapons could serve the United States to send a symbolic message to Iran . The latest armed conflict between the two territories began last February of this year.

The MOAB, or GBU-43/B , is the most powerful non-nuclear bomb in the United States arsenal. It weighs 10,000 kilograms, its blast radius is 1.4 kilometers , and its destructive power is equivalent to eleven tons of TNT . The U.S. military used it for the first time in a real war scenario in April 2017 . At the time, Donald Trump was also the occupant of the White House , and he used it in Afghanistan against the Islamic State.

articles.title: Donald Trump Talks About Sophie Cunningham Again: What Is Their Relationship Really Like?
articles.standfirst: The president introduced her in Montana as a supporter of his movement, although the player has described herself as “right in the middle” and has never publicly confirmed that political endorsement.
articles.summary: The president introduced her in Montana as a supporter of his movement, although the player has described herself as “right in the middle” and has never publicly confirmed that political endorsement.
articles.body:
D onald Trump spoke again about Sophie Cunningham during his rally on October 14 in Kalispell, Montana. Two days after commenting on the player’s attractiveness, the U.S. president claimed he had heard that the Indiana Fever player was “a big fan” of his movement.

Trump again acknowledged that he doesn’t know much about women’s basketball. “I don’t know if she can play,” he said before assuming that she’s probably a good player. But beyond the court, he highlighted what he considers her stance on certain political issues and said that Cunningham brings “sanity.”

Trump portrays Sophie Cunningham as a supporter of his movement

“I like Sophie Cunningham,” Trump said during the event in Montana. He then added that he had heard the player is “a big fan” of him and his movement. His remarks, however, were not backed by any statement from Cunningham in which she publicly identified herself as a Trump supporter.

The distinction is important. Cunningham has indeed expressed views that have found support among conservative circles, particularly her opposition to the participation of transgender women in women’s sports. But when ESPN asked her about her political stance, she described herself as “right in the middle” : she agrees with some ideas from both sides and disagrees with others.

For that reason, the statement made by Trump in Montana should be attributed to the president. There is no statement—at least not publicly—from Cunningham confirming that she is a “big fan” of the movement.

Attention on the player also spread to social media. Trump shared a photo of Cunningham making her well-known finger-pointing gesture, while the official White House account later posted the same image on X. The post once again publicly linked the player to the presidential circle.

The new mention came just two days after the rally held in Youngstown, Ohio. There, Trump had already drawn attention to Cunningham, although on that occasion he spoke mainly about her appearance.

“She’s beautiful,” t he president said before joking with Jon Gruden, a former NFL coach, about the possibility of having her on a team. Trump claimed that her presence could help boost attendance at games, though not necessarily the score.

That statement came after Cunningham gained notoriety for her remarks about the participation of transgender women in women’s sports. Her views drew both criticism and support from conservative circles.

Beyond Trump, how did Cunningham perform on the court?

While her name appears more and more frequently in the president’s speeches, Cunningham also wrapped up a significant season on the court. The guard played in 43 games with the Indiana Fever and averaged 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists, shooting 41.9% from three-point range.

Her performance dipped toward the end of the season, and she averaged 7.3 points in the first-round series against the Las Vegas Aces, in which Indiana was eliminated. Now, she also faces a decision about her future: her contract has expired, and she is an unrestricted free agent.

The relationship between Trump and Cunningham has one clear characteristic: it is the president who has publicly taken the initiative to praise her and associate her with his movement. The player has expressed views that align with parts of the conservative narrative, but she has also identified as a centrist and has not confirmed the political support that Trump attributed to her.

articles.title: In 1965, a $358 million stadium changed the American sports landscape. What happened to it?
articles.standfirst: The Houston Astrodome was considered a marvel of sports architecture and hosted great teams and events. However, decades after its inauguration, it remains closed and its future is still unresolved.
articles.summary: The Houston Astrodome was considered a marvel of sports architecture and hosted great teams and events. However, decades after its inauguration, it remains closed and its future is still unresolved.
articles.body:
The Houston Astrodome, in Texas, was one of the most innovative stadiums of its time. Opened in 1965, it became the first major covered and air-conditioned stadium , a feature that made it possible to enjoy games and shows without depending on the heat, rain, or other weather conditions.

Its construction cost around $35 million, although the total investment and associated works are usually placed at higher figures. Updated to present-day values, the cost cited in some estimates is around $358 million . Known as the "Eighth Wonder of the World," the venue changed the way large stadiums were conceived in the United States.

From historic setting to inactive stadium

The Astrodome was the home of MLB's Houston Astros from 1965 to 1999 and the NFL's Houston Oilers from 1968 to 1996. It also hosted basketball games, concerts, and large-scale shows. In 1992, it even hosted the Republican National Convention.

One of its best-known innovations was the installation of artificial turf in 1966. Natural grass did not thrive under the venue's lighting conditions, so it was replaced by a synthetic surface that eventually became popular under the AstroTurf brand. The solution influenced the design of playing fields in other stadiums.

However, over the years, the Astrodome lost prominence to more modern facilities . The Oilers left in 1996, and the Astros played their last game there in 1999. Although the venue continued to be used for other events, its activity gradually declined until it was left practically empty.

Why did it close its doors?

The turning point came in 2008 , when authorities determined that the Astrodome did not meet fire safety code requirements. The building lost authorization to receive the public and stopped functioning as an event venue.

Since then, Harris County has studied different alternatives to reclaim the space. One of the most ambitious proposals came in 2013: to invest about $217 million to transform it into an exhibition and events center. However, voters rejected the project at the polls.

In 2018, a more affordable alternative was approved, valued at $105 million, which involved raising the floor to street level and building parking underneath . The plan was put on hold in 2019 due to doubts about its feasibility and usefulness once reopened. None of these initiatives was ever carried out.

A future that is still undecided

In November 2024 , the Astrodome Conservancy presented a new proposal to restore the venue. The project, called Vision: Astrodome, envisions a transformation valued at around $1 billion, with retail spaces, restaurants, offices, and cultural areas, in addition to new facilities inside the structure.

The initiative aims to turn the old stadium into a multi-use space and connect it with the rest of the NRG Park complex. However, the proposal needs funding and the backing of the institutions and organizations involved in managing the venue. So far, it has not materialized.

The Astrodome continues to be a symbol of American sports innovation , but it also represents a challenge for Houston authorities: how to preserve a historic structure without taking on a renovation cost that still does not have secured funding.

More than six decades after its inauguration, the stadium is still standing, although without a defined function. Its history left a mark on sports architecture; its next chapter depends on Houston finding a viable way to bring it back to life.

articles.title: Man thought he'd never worry about money again, only to fall into disgrace after winning a $167 million Powerball jackpot
articles.standfirst: James Farthing of Kentucky is squandering a golden opportunity.
articles.summary: James Farthing of Kentucky is squandering a golden opportunity.
articles.body:
When it comes to squandering a golden opportunity, James Farthing is giving everyone a run for their money. Back in April 2025, Farthing was one of the lucky few to win a lottery jackpot: a $167 million check from a Powerball draw.

That type of money should have helped his entire family, plus given him the chance to do whatever he wanted with his life. Instead, Farthing quickly got up to no good. The Kentucky man was arrested not even a week after winning the lottery, for kicking a police officer during an altercation in Pinellas County, Florida.

Kentucky's James Farthing has been arrested five times since winning Powerball

Farthing then got arrested in Kentucky in February of this year for "intimidating a participant in the legal process" . That was followed shortly after by second-degree burglary and marijuana possession charges , stemming from a case which was eventually dismissed.

This past July, Farthing was arrested for first-degree strangulation and fourth-degree assault . Now, his latest arrest came in September, when he was found asleep in a running vehicle in a Walmart parking lot . He was subsequently charged with alcohol intoxication in a public place .

None of these situations have ruined Farthing's life or messed with his newfound wealth in a major way, but the pattern of arrests paint an ominous picture for his future.
